## 9. Canonical Ownership & Compatibility Facades

| Concept | Canonical evidence | Facade/alternative | Decision evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Button/action policy | essentials implementation | primary forwarding files | Keep essentials implementation; time-box root compatibility. |
| Icon | `ui/icons/.../erp-icon.ts` over ng-icons | `HonestyIcon` alias | Keep `ErpIcon` vocabulary; deprecate alias only through a migration. |
| Empty/Error/Loading | essentials implementations | feedback/primary re-exports and contextual renderers | One canonical visual primitive; retain orchestration per pattern. |
| Overlays | essentials Drawer/Modal/Tooltip/support | root facades | Canonicalize import path; do not duplicate focus/stack behavior. |
| Sidebar/navigation | Navigation Tree + Web registry/store for runtime hierarchy | simple Sidebar Item/Section | True capability overlap, not same implementation; review simple family for internalization. |
| UI/Web action policies | UI presentation availability | Web permission/action policy | Keep separate; make adapter terminology explicit. |
| Unsaved changes | UI confirmation surface | Web route guard/coordinator | Keep behavior separation; UI “Guard” naming is misleading. |
| Entity/output actions | Entity Actions, Lifecycle, Bulk, Print/Export, Entity Output | feature execution coordinators | Retain layers; converge vocabulary/placement contracts. |
| Workflow/commercial | generic bases | semantic maintenance/stock and sale/purchase wrappers | Preserve wrappers; consider generic bases internal. |
| Page shell/header/container/footer | Page Shell composes header/container/state | individually exported pieces | Preserve Page Shell; internalize only helpers without supported direct use. |

## 10. Component Layer Classification

Current descriptive layers are: icons → essentials → primary/root → forms/data-display/feedback → business → Web infrastructure/features. Recommended layer values per symbol are in the target CSV. Major current classifications:

- Foundation/token: shared CSS variables, theme selectors, icon contracts.
- Primitives: Button/Icon Button, inputs, Checkbox/Radio/Switch, Money/Date/Status, basic feedback.
- Composites: Select family, Filter Drawer/Bar, Table Toolbar, branch/user/notification controls.
- Generic patterns: Standard Entity Form, Data Page, Smart Table, Page Shell.
- ERP patterns: Entity Directory/Detail/Output, party/address/contact, journal/payment/stock/commercial/workflow editors.
- Application infrastructure: startup/session/branch/permissions/routes/HTTP/offline execution in Web.

The exact classification table is the 532-row public inventory; contracts/services/state are not collapsed into “components”.

## 11. Component Dependency Architecture

**Actual imports/composition:**

```text
ErpEntityDirectory
├─ actions: ErpEntityActions, ErpBulkActionBar, ErpButton
├─ data: ErpSmartTable, ErpCardList, ErpPagination, ErpColumnChooser
├─ filters: ErpFilterBar, ErpFilterDrawer, ErpDateRange, ErpSelect
├─ toolbar: ErpTableToolbar, ErpViewSwitcher, ErpPrintExportActions
├─ display: ErpKpiCard, ErpDateTime, ErpStatusBadge
├─ feedback/overlay: ErpAlert, ErpEmptyState, ErpDrawer
└─ contracts: ErpEntityDirectoryConfig/Event, page/column/sort/selection contracts

ErpEntityDetail
├─ ErpTabs, ErpSectionCard, ErpButton, ErpKpiCard
├─ ErpSmartTable, ErpStatusBadge, ErpAuditTimeline
├─ ErpEmptyState, ErpErrorState
└─ ErpEntitySectionRendererRegistry + custom section outlet

ErpEntitySchemaFields
├─ ErpFormField + ReactiveFormsModule
├─ text/textarea/date/datetime/checkbox/select/remote-select
└─ ErpEntityFieldRendererRegistry + custom field outlet

ErpStandardEntityForm
├─ caller-owned FormGroup and mapping adapter
├─ ErpValidationSummary
└─ ErpFormActions

ErpSmartTable
├─ ErpCheckbox, SortHeader, Pagination
├─ DateTime, StatusBadge, HonestyIcon
└─ column/data-page/page-request/selection contracts
```

Select uses option-list/store behavior and overlays; Remote Select adds data-source/hydration/cancellation contracts; Multi Select adds chip/multiple-value behavior. Shell composes projected topbar/sidebar/footer rather than importing Web features. Authorization gates accept resolved decisions and project content. No cycles were confirmed. The semantic reverse-layer concern is root Shell/System acting as a dependency of forms/data/business through the root barrel.

## 12. Duplicate & Overlap Findings

Exactly nine evidence-backed groups:

1. primary compatibility facades vs secondary entry points;
2. Empty/Error symbols across essentials/feedback;
3. `ErpIcon` vs `HonestyIcon` alias vocabulary;
4. UI Action Policy vs Web Permission Action Policy;
5. UI Unsaved Changes “Guard” vs Web route guard/coordinator;
6. Sidebar Item/Section vs Navigation Tree;
7. Entity Actions / Print-Export / Entity Output overlap;
8. canonical feedback vs Smart Table/Card/Directory contextual states;
9. generic workflow/commercial bases vs semantic wrappers.

Evidence and migration status are recorded per public symbol. These are not nine delete candidates: several are legitimate cross-layer adaptations or wrappers.

## 13. Boundary Violations

### Confirmed major violations — exactly 2

1. **UI ERP business components bypass UI primitives.** `ui/business` files for commercial, journal, stock, report, workflow and permission interactions contain native controls even though the package can compose forms/essentials. Consequence: duplicated focus/theme/RTL/validation behavior.
2. **Web feature pages bypass the design system.** exact counts and representative paths are in section 14. Customers do not exhibit these bypasses, proving the target composition is viable.

### Questionable boundaries requiring decision

- primary/root mixes foundational contracts with Shell/System components;
- generic Entity Directory/Detail are located beside domain business editors;
- `FinancialDataGuard` is a presentation component whose name implies enforcement;
- System/Sync/Offline presentation is bundled into UI while execution belongs to Web;
- compatibility barrel exports make accidental coupling easy.

No UI→API Client or UI→Web violation exists.

## 14. Design-System Bypass Findings

| Scope/classification | Button | Select | Non-checkbox input | Checkbox | Radio | Textarea | Native dialog |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Web design-system bypass | 32 | 45 | 35 | 32 | 0 | 3 | 0 |
| UI business-pattern bypass | 88 | 7 | 27 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Correct UI primitive internals | 9 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 0 |

The generator also identifies one correct native table inside a UI primitive; Web native tables are print/static strings and must not be confused with live design-system bypasses. Representative Web concentrations: maintenance intake, setup services, spare-parts, ink-products, stabilizers, bootstrap setup, stock transfer and inventory dashboard. Exact files/occurrences are in `audit-artifacts/data/public-api.json`/`audit-summary.json` and source scan artifacts.

## 15. Forms Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Schema[Entity Form Schema] --> Fields[Entity Schema Fields]
  Registry[Field Renderer Registry] --> Fields
  Fields --> Controls[Text/Date/Select/Checkbox/etc.]
  Form[Caller FormGroup] --> Standard[Standard Entity Form]
  Standard --> Validation[Validation Summary / server mapping]
  Standard --> Actions[Form Actions]
  Feature[Feature state/workflow/adapter] --> Form
  Feature --> Schema
  Feature --> Registry
  Feature --> Wizard[Stepper / review / wizard state]
  Feature --> Unsaved[Web unsaved-change coordinator]
  Feature --> Concurrency[Web row-version + UI conflict dialog]
```

The repository already has a Form Engine, but it is distributed rather than one God Component. Reactive Forms/FormGroup stay caller-owned. `ErpStandardEntityForm` owns submit mapping, blocking/failure events, actions and validation summary. `ErpEntitySchemaFields` renders schema fields. Supported schema field kinds are text, textarea, date, datetime, select, remote-select, checkbox and custom. Metadata includes IDs/control names, label/hint/placeholder/layout, required/visible/readonly/disabled predicates, select options/size, remote source, checkbox size/variant, and custom renderer key/input resolution. Steps and review groups are separately modeled.

Conditional rules are typed callback predicates/text resolvers receiving value/context/FormGroup. **INFERENCE:** this is expressive code, not a serialized mini-language; complexity risk arises from callback proliferation, but no expression parser/DSL exists. Custom fields use `ErpEntityFieldRendererRegistry` and `ErpEntityCustomFieldOutlet`; custom sections and transaction editors allow complete opt-out.

| Form | Architecture | Schema/custom behavior | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer create/edit | 358-line page + state/workflow/models/schema/adapter/renderers | schema-driven conventional fields plus custom renderers/review | Golden reference; callback/context complexity to monitor. |
| Supplier form | 1,328-line page | mixed feature-local markup/state/API | Legacy page-centric; duplicated UX logic. |
| Stock transfer | 962-line page + ERP stock workflow/editor pieces | complex transaction composition, not forced into entity schema | Correct opt-out direction; native-control adoption gaps remain. |

Server validation is mapped into validation issues/summary; backend validation and permission decisions remain Web-owned. Unsaved routing is Web-owned. Concurrency combines UI dialog contracts with feature/API row-version execution.

## 16. Selection Controls Architecture

| Control | Intended repository use | Data/search model | Interaction/limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ErpSelect` | finite local option selection | local options, search/filter/group/sort, icons/images, disabled, clear, templating | keyboard/focus/open overlay; five sizes; no server paging. |
| `ErpMultiSelect` | finite multiple selection | local list + chips/groups/search | multiple values/clear; no virtualization proven. |
| `ErpRemoteSelect` | server-backed/entity lookup | typed data source, search, hydration of unknown selected value, cancellation/stale protection | loading/no results/errors; server paging capability is contract-dependent; no virtual scroll proven. |
| option-list infrastructure | shared behavior/store | normalized options/filter state/active item | internal composition candidate. |

No separate public Autocomplete/Combobox/EntityPicker symbol was confirmed. The repository distinction is local single, local multiple, and remote single. That is sufficient until a concrete usage proves another semantic control is needed. Axe currently finds missing accessible names on several select examples/page-size fields and target-size failure on two clear buttons; these are real interaction-quality defects.

## 17. Data Explorer / Smart Table Architecture

- Data-source/page contracts define request, result, sort, pagination, row identity and load state without URLs/HTTP.
- `ErpDataPage` owns request execution lifecycle, stale cancellation, retries, safe errors and optional previous-data retention.
- `ErpSmartTable` owns table rendering, column definitions, sort intent, selection and pagination composition; it emits events and does not fetch.
- Card List, Column Chooser, Filter Bar/Drawer, Table Toolbar, View Switcher, Pagination and KPI remain separately exported/composable.
- Entity Directory coordinates these pieces and one typed event union; feature state/API remains caller-owned.

```text
Feature API adapter -> feature query/state -> ErpEntityDirectory config
  -> ErpSmartTable OR projected ErpCardList
  -> page/sort/filter/view/selection/output event
  -> feature validates contextKey + permission
  -> state/API request
  -> immutable snapshot/summary back to Directory
```

Server-side pagination/sort/filter is the normal flow. Local option filtering belongs to selection controls; Smart Table does not know customer/supplier URLs. Visible-column persistence is caller/application responsibility; Directory controls chooser intent. The ecosystem is a coherent Data Explorer pattern, not a single universal Smart Table, but contextual loading/empty/error rendering overlaps feedback primitives.

## 18. Entity Directory Architecture

`ErpEntityDirectoryConfig` is opt-in and presentation-only: control/context IDs, snapshot/load state, page request, row identity, columns, table/cards view, optional pagination/summary/toolbar/selection/bulk/filters/notices/result/empty state. Its one `changed` output is a discriminated event union for refresh/retry/page/sort/view/selection/columns/filter/output/action intents. Comments explicitly state context keys are epochs, not authority; callers recheck context and permissions.

At 462 TS lines it is a major coordinator, but it composes focused children rather than embedding API logic. Strengths: explicit unknown totals, context-key protection, caller-owned filters, projected card/result templates, permission-neutral events. Risks: very wide configuration/event contracts and dual use of Drawer/FilterDrawer/fields. Recommendation: preserve behavior, refine API/group ownership, redesign visuals only after tokens/primitives.

## 19. Entity Detail Architecture

`ErpEntityDetail` renders a typed schema: hero/actions, facts, KPIs, rails, status, tabs, audit timeline and table/custom sections. `ErpEntitySectionRendererRegistry` provides feature-owned custom sections without importing the feature. It composes `ErpSectionCard`, Tabs, KPI, Smart Table, Status, Empty/Error and Audit Timeline.

Customer Detail proves the intended mapping: page 235 lines, presenter 291, state 185, schema 366, actions 268 plus adapters/renderers. **OBSERVED:** the current three-column layout wastes a large lower rail and wraps central values at 1440/1024; this is a template/SCSS redesign issue, not evidence that registry/schema logic should be replaced.

## 20. Action Framework

Repository concepts cover action ID, label, icon, tone, variant/placement, visibility, disabled/busy/reason, confirmation policy, lifecycle transitions, idempotency reservation, bulk actions and output scope. Permission/capability/branch/online resolution lives in Web.

```text
UI/feature action definition
 -> Web PermissionActionPolicy resolves authority/capability/branch/online
 -> ErpResolvedAction availability
 -> Button / IconButton / ActionMenu / EntityActions / Lifecycle / Bulk / Output
 -> invocation event
 -> optional ConfirmationDialog
 -> feature async/idempotency lock
 -> API/output coordinator
 -> result notice/error/concurrency state
```

UI Action Policy is presentation data; “Action Security” is tested behavior, not a production class. Entity Actions controls common slots/placement; Lifecycle adds transitions/idempotency; Print/Export adds scopes/options; Entity Output provides safe CSV/HTML generation; Web coordinators perform backend-aware execution. The canonical vocabulary already emerging is Definition → Availability/Resolved Action → Invocation → Confirmation → Execution Result. Consolidate terminology/adapters, not layers.

## 21. Authorization Architecture

Actual enforcement is backend. Web frontend policy uses permission surface/models, field policies, navigation pruning, route guards, active branch/session context and HTTP forbidden/session handling. UI gates only render resolved state:

- `ErpPermissionGate`: hide/disable presentation.
- `ErpBranchScopeGate`: hide/disable/readonly decision presentation.
- `ErpFinancialDataGuard`: projects allowed/fallback templates; name overstates its enforcement role.

Customer list/form/detail use feature policies/resolved actions and field behavior. Supplier/Admin screens use older mixed policies/markup, so flow is less uniform. The authenticated HTTP chain attaches authentication and current branch context; startup/session/branch orchestrators centralize refresh/login/re-entry behavior. Visibility and disabled state must never be described as security enforcement.

## 22. Shell Architecture

`ErpAppShell` composes projected Topbar, Sidebar, content and footer, provides skip link, fixed desktop grid and modal-navigation focus/overlay behavior below 61.99rem. Auth Shell and System Page Shell handle separate unauthenticated/system states. `ErpPageShell` composes breadcrumbs, Page Header, state feedback and content surface. Header/Footer/Section Card/Tabs/branch/user/notifications/search/theme toggle remain focused pieces.

**OBSERVED:** shell works in both themes and all captured widths. At 1024 it retains the fixed sidebar and compresses content. Shell does not import feature modules; Web authenticated workspace wires feature-aware navigation/session data.

## 23. Navigation Architecture

Web `NavigationRegistry` builds permission-visible nodes; UI `ErpNavigationTree` renders links/groups and emits expansion. `WorkspaceNavigationStore` owns active URL, expanded IDs and localStorage persistence keyed by system instance/user/branch, sanitizes stored IDs and reveals route ancestors. Legacy `/workspace/*` URLs are mapped to canonical modular routes by `route-catalog.ts`.

Route activation is real through RouterLink/Angular Router. Simple `ErpSidebarItem/Section` coexist but do not provide the richer registry/store behavior. Technical validation permits deeper nesting; the normal maximum-three-level rule remains content governance, not a renderer limitation.

## 24. Feedback Architecture

Alert, Confirmation, Concurrency Conflict, Empty, Error, Loading, Skeleton, Offline Banner, Offline Workspace Banner and Sync Center are public. They emit user intent and do not execute backend work. Empty/Error are exported through overlapping entry points; Smart Table/Card/Directory also orchestrate contextual states. Canonical visuals should be shared while contextual load logic stays in the pattern.

## 25. Overlay Architecture

Drawer, Modal and Tooltip use shared overlay activation/top-stack/focus-trap support. App Shell overlay navigation uses the same focus principles. Action Menu positions a fixed surface, supports keyboard Home/End/Arrow/Escape/Tab and restores focus. Tooltip supports pointer and focus behavior. **OBSERVED:** modal/drawer/select/tooltip open states render in both themes; no stacking/runtime error was captured. Do not duplicate overlay infrastructure in feature pages.

## 26. ERP Business Components

Generic ERP patterns: Entity Directory, Entity Detail, Entity Output, Audit Timeline, Attachment/party presentations. Domain editors: Commercial/Sale/Purchase Lines, Journal Lines, Payment Allocation, Stock Adjustment, Permission Tree, Report Filter Panel and workflow wrappers.

Largest UI sources include Commercial Lines 561, Party Address 518, Party Contact 515, Stock Adjustment 385, Repeater 383, Report Filter 368, Workflow 366, Permission Tree 333 and Journal Lines 324 lines. Size alone is not a defect. Confirmed native controls inside higher-layer editors are the defect; preserve business behavior and compose established primitives. Semantic wrappers should remain; generic bases are internalization candidates.

## 27. Application/System Infrastructure

Web owns startup probes/orchestration, authentication/session expiry/multi-tab coordination, active branch, interceptors, permission resolution, unsaved route coordination, feature APIs, output execution and row-version concurrency. UI owns presentation endpoints such as backend unavailable, forbidden, initialization required and session expiry.

Sync Center/offline surfaces exist; a complete generic offline execution queue was not proven. Task Center was not found as a dedicated system. These are “not proven implemented”, not deletion candidates.

## 32. SCSS Architecture

`ui/src/styles/_index.scss` forwards tokens/themes/foundation/entity styles; component SCSS is mostly colocated; Web and Showcase import shared styles plus application/page styles. Logical properties and BEM-like naming are common and beneficial. Fragmentation comes from inline component styles, page-local values, uncontrolled breakpoints/radii/colors and limited token centralization.

Comprehensive scope: 191 style-bearing sources (41 SCSS + 150 inline styles, 188 owning files). The exact token/literal tables are in `ERP_UI_TOKEN_INVENTORY.md`.

## 33. Design Tokens

| Measure | Exact comprehensive count |
|---|---:|
| Declared custom-property names | 123 |
| Used custom-property names | 155 |
| Literal color occurrences / distinct | 257 / 102 |
| Radius declarations / distinct values | 510 / 39 |
| z-index declarations / distinct values | 38 / 17 |
| Media queries | 173 |
| `!important` | 27 |

Missing/locally unresolved names include control/ripple/tooltip positioning and several `--honesty-*` variables in narrower scopes. Checkbox, Radio, Select, KPI and Tooltip define sizeable component-local mini-token systems. These are useful experiments but not yet a unified foundation. Repeated literal values should first be categorized semantically; do not replace every number with a token mechanically.

## 34. Theme Architecture

Light/Dark are CSS custom-property themes, not duplicate component implementations. **OBSERVED:** main Showcase/Customer scenarios render coherently in both. **STATIC EVIDENCE:** component-local hex/RGBA fallbacks and Web/page styles can bypass themes. Theme redesign should freeze semantic roles (canvas/surface/elevated/border/text/action/status/focus) before component SCSS changes.

## 35. RTL Architecture

Arabic/RTL is the default rendered direction. Logical properties are widely used; Navigation/App Shell explicitly handle RTL transforms. **OBSERVED:** all 56 fresh captures are RTL and main alignment is correct. Risks: physical left/right remains in overlay positioning and legacy styles, native date placeholder remains English, and visual regression coverage includes historic LTR references that are compatibility evidence rather than product priority.

## 36. Responsive Architecture

Desktop priorities 1920/1440/1366/1024 were captured. Existing quality tests additionally cover 360/390/768 and pass responsive assertions, but mobile Web is not redesign priority. App Shell overlay breakpoint is below 61.99rem; thus 1024 retains a fixed sidebar. **OBSERVED blocker:** Customer table clips at 1024. Breakpoint fragmentation (173 media queries) means responsive behavior is not governed centrally.

## 37. HTML / Internal Design Reference Audit

Exactly 29 HTML files exist, all Angular app/component templates or app indices; no separate static HTML reference project exists in the repository. Eight document screenshots under `docs/frontend/angular-web-rebuild/gemini-review-2026-09-05/architecture-alignment/customer-gold-completion/evidence/` represent GS02/GS03 list/detail/form/showcase evidence. Committed Playwright snapshots and live Showcase are the other valid internal visual references. They are evidence, not automatically approved design.

Documentation authority is contradictory: `docs/README.md` says React is final and Angular frozen, while `docs/frontend/angular/ANGULAR.md` says Angular is the primary active client and contains stale ports/test/environment details. This is a High governance risk requiring a human source-of-truth decision.

## 45. Dependency Residue

Potential residue with no direct source/test/tool textual import found includes Angular animations/platform-browser-dynamic, Tajawal font, Lordicon, ng-bootstrap, NgRx Store, ngx-translate packages, Popper, angularx-flatpickr/flatpickr, legacy Jasmine/Karma packages, Lottie, ngx-cookie-service, ngx-csv, simplebar and SweetAlert2. `zone.js` and `browserslist` may act through runtime/config conventions; “no import” is not proof of removal safety. Bootstrap substring matches require import-specific follow-up. No package was removed.

The 51 npm advisories increase review urgency but package changes belong to a separately planned dependency/security pass.

## 46. Strong Existing Work to Preserve

1. UI/backend independence: UI has no API/HTTP/Web dependency.
2. `ErpIcon` semantic façade: vendor packs remain internal/tree-shakeable.
3. Permission split: Web resolves, UI presents.
4. Generated API boundary and checks.
5. cancellable/stale-safe Data Page and Remote Select contracts.
6. schema forms with registry/custom escape hatch.
7. composable Smart Table ecosystem rather than backend-aware monolith.
8. Customer decomposition into page/state/workflow/presenter/schema/adapter.
9. Entity Detail custom section registry.
10. navigation persistence scoped by instance/user/branch.
11. startup/session/active-branch/interceptor orchestration.
12. concurrency dialog vs Web row-version execution split.
13. Entity Output CSV formula escaping, RFC 4180 and HTML XSS escaping.
14. architecture, API, icon, page, unit, E2E and visual governance.

## 47. Current Architecture Model

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  O[OpenAPI] --> API[Generated API Client]
  API --> FA[Web feature adapters/services]
  R[Startup/session/branch/permission/HTTP] --> FP[Web feature pages]
  FA --> FP
  I[Icons/Essentials/Root] --> F[Forms]
  I --> D[Data Display]
  I --> FB[Feedback]
  F --> B[Business patterns]
  D --> B
  FB --> B
  B --> FP
  I --> S[Shell]
  S --> FP
  FP --> MOD[Modern decomposed Customers]
  FP --> LEG[Legacy page-centric features]
```

Current form, data, actions, permissions and navigation flows are documented in sections 15–23. This factual model contains both modern and legacy eras; it is not the target architecture.

## 48. Recommended Target Layering

| Target layer | Existing candidates | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Foundation | semantic tokens/themes/type/spacing/motion/breakpoints/icon contracts | one governed vocabulary |
| Primitives | Button/Icon/Input/Checkbox/Radio/Switch/Status/basic display | stable small controls |
| Forms | CVA base, fields, selects, upload/repeater, validation | form behavior without entity semantics |
| Data | data contracts/display/table/pagination/chooser/card | backend-neutral state/display |
| Feedback | alert/states/dialog visuals | canonical response visuals |
| Overlays | drawer/modal/tooltip/focus/stack | one interaction infrastructure |
| Navigation | node contracts/tree/state | route-independent hierarchy |
| Composite | filter/toolbar/branch/user/notifications | focused multi-primitive assemblies |
| Generic patterns | Standard Entity Form, Data Explorer, wizard/review | repeated UX without domain DTOs |
| Shell | app/auth/system/page/topbar/sidebar/header/footer | application framing only |
| ERP Business UI | Entity Directory/Detail/Output, party/journal/payment/stock/workflow | reusable ERP semantics |
| Application/System | startup/session/branch/permissions/guards/HTTP/sync execution | backend/environment awareness |
| Features | customer/supplier/etc. adapters/workflows/pages | domain execution and mapping |

## 49. Public API Target Summary

The full 532-row recommendation is `ERP_UI_PUBLIC_API_TARGET_MAP.csv`. Priority: choose one canonical entry point per symbol; retain compatibility through explicit timed facades; internalize implementation helpers/bases; move generic Entity patterns out of domain-business naming if the package structure changes; never put API/permission execution into UI. No API migration occurred during the audit.

## 50. Component Decision Summary

`ERP_UI_COMPONENT_DECISION_MATRIX.md` contains 120 canonical component/directive rows with logic, architecture, rendered status, reuse, adoption, duplication risk and one allowed action. Broad conclusion: preserve behavior for primitives/forms/data/shell/entity patterns; redesign visual SCSS/tokens; refine canonical pattern APIs; compose business editors from primitives; internalize unsupported helpers/generic bases; require evidence before replacement.

## 51. Page/Pattern Target Map

Lists/details/conventional forms should migrate to the Customer-backed Entity patterns after Customer gold is frozen. Dashboards should reuse KPI/data/shell but retain feature metric composition. Transactions should use semantic line/allocation/stock/workflow editors plus feature-specific calculations rather than expanding Entity Form schema into a language. Reports should compose Report Filter/Data/Output. Approval/workflow screens should use semantic workflow components with feature lifecycle execution.

Zero duplicated UX logic—not zero-code pages—is the target.

## 53. Technical Risk Model

No Critical issue was proven. Seven High risks:

1. **Public API ambiguity:** 532 rows/525 symbols, duplicate ownership/facades. Scaling consequence: incompatible imports/versioning.
2. **Parallel feature architectures:** 1,000–1,963-line pages beside decomposed Customers. Consequence: every UX change is reimplemented.
3. **Primitive bypass at UI business and Web:** exact native counts in section 14. Consequence: accessibility/theme/RTL drift.
4. **Action/output model drift:** UI/Web/entity/lifecycle/bulk/output concepts lack one explicit adapter vocabulary.
5. **Theme/token fragmentation:** 102 colors, 39 radii, 17 z-index values, 173 media queries. Consequence: redesign cannot remain consistent.
6. **Documentation authority conflict:** React-frozen vs Angular-primary documents and stale commands. Consequence: future agents may select the wrong frontend/commands.
7. **Visual quality gates not green:** Showcase baseline and Axe failures plus 1024 clipping. Consequence: current visuals cannot be blessed as golden.

Medium risks: package residue/advisories, wide Directory/Form contracts, mixed generic/domain business package, limited exhaustive Showcase coverage, sync/offline behavior not fully proven. Low risks: compatibility naming and small local style hacks.

## 54. Open Human Decisions

1. Which document is authoritative: Angular primary or React replacement?
2. Canonical UI entry-point naming and deprecation window.
3. Whether Entity Directory/Detail belong to generic patterns or ERP Business UI package.
4. Whether simple Sidebar family remains supported.
5. exact normal desktop shell behavior at 1024.
6. breadcrumb placement and Topbar density.
7. drawer logical side in RTL.
8. final semantic visual token palette/density/radii/elevation.
9. whether target-size Axe rule is mandatory product policy; accessible naming is interaction correctness regardless.
10. dependency/security remediation scope and compatibility budget.

## 55. Recommended Implementation Sequence

1. **Build/tooling stabilization:** commit four audited fixes; keep all builds/serve green. Gate: clean clone runs build/unit/Web E2E.
2. **Architecture boundary decisions:** approve layer/package ownership. Do not move files yet.
3. **Public API decisions:** canonical entry points + compatibility plan. Gate: consumer graph and migration tests.
4. **Token redesign:** semantic color/type/space/radius/elevation/z/breakpoint/density. Do not change pattern APIs.
5. **Primitive visual redesign:** Button/Icon/inputs/select/checkbox/radio/switch/status. Gate: Showcase Light/Dark/RTL/keyboard and approved baselines.
6. **Composite redesign:** overlays, feedback, filter, toolbar, page/header controls. Gate: interaction/quality suite.
7. **Pattern redesign:** Table/Data Explorer/Page Shell/Entity patterns. Gate: 1024/1366/1440/1920 and state matrices.
8. **Golden-feature validation:** Customers only until list/form/detail/output/actions/permissions/visuals are signed off.
9. **CRUD migration:** suppliers/users/roles then similar entities via common patterns; one feature per bounded package.
10. **Complex transaction validation:** stock/maintenance/journal/payment; preserve opt-out/custom logic.
11. **Gradual feature migration:** retire native bypasses and God pages with regression gates.
12. **Compatibility cleanup:** remove facades/legacy only after telemetry/search and versioned deprecation gates.

Each phase must preserve the previous green gates; visual baseline updates require explicit approved-design evidence, not “make test pass”.

# ERP UI Architecture Audit

> **Audit scope:** read-only architectural audit of the Angular frontend as found on 2026-09-20. No production source, configuration, style, dependency, or public API was changed. This report is the only repository artifact created or updated by the audit.
>
> **Evidence standard:** findings are based on workspace configuration, declarations, imports and usages, SCSS/templates, architecture checks, routes, and committed Playwright tests/baselines. Fresh rendered inspection was attempted but was not reliable: the clean workspace's `start:ui-showcase:serve` target resolves `honesty-erp-ui/*` through absent `dist` packages. The audit did not build or change the workspace to work around this because only this report may change.

## 1. Executive Summary

The frontend is a four-project Angular workspace on Angular **21.2.x** and TypeScript **5.9.3**, not approximately Angular 22: generated API client (`honesty-api-client`), reusable UI library (`honesty-erp-ui`), UI reference application (`honesty-erp-ui-showcase`), and ERP application (`honesty-erp-web`). The UI library has a primary entry point and six secondary entry points: `essentials`, `icons`, `forms`, `data-display`, `feedback`, and `business`. Evidence: `src/frontend/angular/angular.json`, `package.json`, and the UI `ng-package.json`/`public-api.ts` files.

This codebase should not be rewritten wholesale. Strong foundations include presentation-only UI authorization gates, the Web permission engine, generated-contract isolation, cancellable/retryable data-source contracts, the schema-form renderer registry and custom escape hatch, customer feature decomposition, permission-aware navigation, startup/session/branch orchestration, and visual/accessibility tests. Those behaviors deserve preservation even if the visual system changes.

The main architectural problem is **uneven adoption**. Customers compose `ErpEntityDirectory`, `ErpStandardEntityForm`, `ErpEntityDetail`, presenters, state/workflow collaborators, and dedicated output/action services. Many older features still contain 1,000–1,900 line page classes and direct native controls. Two implementation eras therefore coexist inside Web.

The UI package is broader than a stable external-style package should be. Static export traversal found approximately **473 unique public symbols** across seven entry points. Several symbols are exposed through multiple entry points (`ErpEmptyState`, `ErpErrorState`, `ErpIconSource`, and related types), and compatibility aliases/facades blur canonical ownership. The architecture checker nevertheless confirms an acyclic entry-point direction.

No UI-to-API-client or UI-to-Web import was found. The two confirmed major boundary violations are downward bypasses: ERP business components directly implement native controls instead of consistently composing UI primitives, and numerous Web features do the same at page level. Action, unsaved-changes, output, navigation, and feedback areas contain overlaps, but several are deliberate layers rather than interchangeable duplicates.

The visual system is fragmented. Across 424 production UI/Web style-bearing files, the audit counted 493 hex-color occurrences, 49 `rgb`/`rgba` occurrences, 26 `!important` occurrences, 1,957 `rem` occurrences, 984 `px` occurrences, and 39 distinct media-query breakpoints. The central token file contains about 48 definitions, while 32 referenced `--honesty-*` variables are not declared there. The Web global body background also hard-codes `#f3f3f9`, bypassing theme canvas behavior.

Fresh rendered visual inspection was **not** reliable. Committed Playwright baselines for checkbox, radio, select, tooltip, empty state, KPI, and customer 360 provide partial rendered evidence. Section 18 distinguishes that evidence from source-inferred inconsistency.

Headline counts:

- Angular projects: **4**.
- Approximate unique UI public exports: **473**.
- Suspected duplicate/overlap groups: **9**.
- Confirmed major boundary violations: **2**.
- High-risk areas: **6**; no issue is labelled Critical without executable production proof.
- Confirmed dead UI declarations: **0**; potentially unused public declarations: **2**.

## 2. Workspace Architecture

### 2.1 Important tree

```text
Honesty ERP/
├─ ERP_UI_ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT.md              # this report
├─ docs/                                     # architectural/project documentation
└─ src/frontend/angular/
   ├─ angular.json                           # four projects and targets
   ├─ package.json                           # scripts/dependencies
   ├─ tsconfig.json                          # aliases/project references
   ├─ tools/                                 # architecture/governance checks
   ├─ e2e/ and e2e-showcase/                 # Playwright suites/baselines
   ├─ api-client/
   │  └─ src/{lib,public-api.ts}             # generated API surface
   ├─ ui/
   │  ├─ src/                                # primary API: actions/auth/shell/system
   │  ├─ essentials/                         # tokens/basic controls/layout
   │  ├─ icons/                              # semantic ng-icons integration
   │  ├─ forms/                              # controls/form engine/workflow
   │  ├─ data-display/                       # table/data/directory components
   │  ├─ feedback/                           # states/overlays/feedback
   │  └─ business/                           # ERP-specific patterns/editors
   ├─ ui-showcase/src/app/                   # catalog/playgrounds
   └─ web/src/app/
      ├─ auth/ and core/                     # shell/session/startup/permissions
      ├─ features/sales/customers/           # current golden-standard feature
      ├─ suppliers/, employees/, maintenance/, inventory/, ...
      └─ app.routes.ts                       # application route composition
```

### 2.2 Projects and roles

| Project | Kind | Source root | Principal entry | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `honesty-api-client` | library | `api-client/src` | `api-client/src/public-api.ts` | OpenAPI-generated DTOs, functions and services. |
| `honesty-erp-ui` | library with secondary entry points | `ui` | `ui/src/public-api.ts` plus six secondary APIs | Design system, generic patterns, shell, ERP patterns, system UI. |
| `honesty-erp-ui-showcase` | application | `ui-showcase/src` | `ui-showcase/src/main.ts` | Reference/playground and visual behavior verification. |
| `honesty-erp-web` | application | `web/src` | `web/src/main.ts`, `app.config.ts`, `app.routes.ts` | Actual ERP and backend-aware orchestration. |

`angular.json` defines build/serve/test targets. Workspace scripts in `package.json` distinguish dependency-building commands from direct serve commands. The direct Showcase serve attempt failed because imports such as `honesty-erp-ui/forms` resolve through distribution paths while those packages were absent; dependency-aware build scripts are therefore part of the effective build contract.

Important dependencies include Angular 21.2.x packages, TypeScript 5.9.3, RxJS, `@ng-icons/core` 34.x plus icon packs, Cairo/Tajawal font packages, ng-packagr, Karma/Jasmine and Playwright/Axe test tooling. Several UI framework/helper packages have no non-test source imports and are listed conservatively as potential residue in section 22 rather than assumed dependencies or deleted candidates.

### 2.3 Package aliases and styling entry points

`src/frontend/angular/tsconfig.json` maps package imports for `honesty-api-client`, `honesty-erp-ui`, and secondary entry points to built `dist` entry points. UI exposes `essentials`, `icons`, `forms`, `data-display`, `feedback`, and `business` in addition to the primary package. The packaging boundary is real, but the primary API also re-exports compatibility facades, so canonical ownership is not yet unequivocal.

The central SCSS entry is `ui/src/styles/_index.scss`, forwarding tokens, themes, foundations, and entity styles. Core theme sources include `ui/src/styles/_tokens.scss` and `ui/src/styles/_themes.scss`; component SCSS is colocated. Web and Showcase consume these shared styles, while Web also has global feature/application styles.

No confirmed circular entry-point dependency was found. A design question remains: the primary/root entry point owns shell, actions, authorization presentation and system UI while apparently lower packages depend on it, so it is not a pure Foundation layer.

| Journal Lines Editor | ERP Business Component | `ui/business/src/lib/erp-journal-lines-editor.ts` | Yes | forms/data | accounting transactions | ERP Business UI | Domain-specific by design. |

| Payment Allocation/Stock Adjustment | ERP Business Components | `ui/business/src/lib/erp-payment-allocation-editor.ts`, `erp-stock-adjustment-editor.ts` | Yes | forms/data | finance/inventory | ERP Business UI | Correctly domain-scoped but uses native controls internally. |
| Permission Tree | ERP Business/System Component | `ui/business/src/lib/erp-permission-tree.ts` | Yes | checkbox/forms | roles/permissions | ERP Business UI | Domain application control, not generic tree primitive. |
| Report Filter Panel | ERP Business Pattern | `ui/business/src/lib/erp-report-filter-panel.ts` | Yes | form controls | reports | ERP Business UI | Higher-order report composition. |
| Workflow panels and semantic wrappers | ERP Business Pattern | `ui/business/src/lib/erp-workflow-panels.ts` plus stock-transfer/maintenance wrappers | Yes | actions/forms/feedback | workflows | ERP Business UI | Base/wrappers are intentional but public scope needs review. |
| Entity Output/Print-Export Actions | ERP Pattern + Contracts | `ui/business/src/lib/erp-entity-output.ts` and print/export files | Yes | actions/menu | entity lists/details | ERP Business UI | Overlaps placement/scope responsibilities with Entity Actions. |
| Action Policy contracts | Contract / Type | `ui/essentials/src/lib/actions/erp-action-policy.ts` with root façade | Yes | icons/semantic variants | action components/features | Generic Action Infrastructure | Presentation-neutral; authority is resolved outside components. |
| Action Menu/Entity Actions/Lifecycle Actions/Bulk Action Bar | Composite/ERP Patterns | `ui/src/lib/actions/*` | Yes | policies/buttons/menus | directories/details/workflows | Actions / ERP Patterns | Distinct placements; share resolved-action vocabulary. |
| Async action lock/idempotency utilities | State + Utility | `ui/src/lib/actions/*` | Yes | in-memory state/key generation | action workflows | Action Infrastructure | Client reservation is not server idempotency enforcement. |
| UI Unsaved Changes Guard | Feedback/Overlay Component | `ui/src/lib/actions` or forms façade | Yes | modal/action UI | form workflow | UI Pattern | Despite its name, it is not the Web router guard. |
| Permission Gate/Branch Scope Gate/Financial Data Guard | Authorization presentation components | `ui/src/lib/authorization/erp-*.ts` | Yes | content projection/input state | Web/templates | Authorization UI | Display gates only; no API/permission-service coupling. |
| Drawer/Modal/Tooltip | Overlay Components/Directive | `ui/essentials/src/lib/overlays/*` with root facades | Yes | CDK-like DOM behavior/icons | forms, menus, filters | Overlays/Primitives | Tooltip supports pointer/focus behavior. |
| Alert/Confirmation/Concurrency Dialog | Feedback Components | `ui/feedback/src/lib/erp-alert.ts`, `erp-confirmation-dialog.ts`, `erp-concurrency-conflict-dialog.ts` | Yes | modal/buttons | Web workflows | Feedback | Concurrency is application-aware feedback but backend-neutral. |
| Empty/Error/Loading/Skeleton | Feedback Components | `ui/feedback/src/lib/*` and essentials versions/facades | Yes, duplicate paths | icons/buttons | data/forms/pages | Feedback | Canonical ownership is ambiguous. |

| App/Auth/System Page Shells | Shell Components | `ui/src/lib/shells/*` and system page support | Yes | navigation/feedback/content projection | Web/Showcase/system pages | Shell | Distinct page contexts are justified. |
| Sidebar/Sidebar Item/Sidebar Section | Navigation/Shell Components | `ui/src/lib/shells/erp-sidebar*.ts` | Yes | icons/buttons | primarily Showcase/legacy shell | Shell | Simpler system coexists with Navigation Tree. |
| Navigation Tree contracts/state | Navigation Components + Contracts + State | `ui/src/lib/navigation/*` | Yes | icons/actions | Web authenticated shell, Showcase | Navigation/Shell | Supports nested nodes and controlled expansion. |
| Topbar/Page Header/Footer/Page Shell/Section Card | Shell/Composite Components | `ui/src/lib/shells/erp-*.ts` | Yes | actions/navigation/content slots | Web and Showcase | Shell | No separate dedicated “Short Header” declaration found. |
| Breadcrumbs/Tabs/Branch Selector/User Menu/Notification Bell/Global Search/Theme Toggle | Shell Components | `ui/src/lib/shells/erp-*.ts` | Yes | primitives/overlays/icons | Web shell/Showcase | Shell | They emit events and remain backend-neutral. |
| Backend Unavailable/Forbidden/Initialization Required/Session Expiry | System Page/Feedback Components | `ui/src/lib/system/*` | Yes | system shell/actions | startup/session Web flows | Application/System UI | Initialization Required had no direct Web/Showcase consumer found. |
| Guards, services, pipes in UI | Classification result | entire `ui/**` | None found as Angular route guards, injectable services, or pipes | — | — | — | State managers/stores are plain classes; actual guards/services live in Web. |

The inventory confirms the requested concepts largely exist. Additional explicit results are: `ErpAsyncContent` exists at `ui/feedback/src/lib/erp-async-content.ts`; `ErpContactField` exists at `ui/data-display/src/lib/erp-contact-field.ts`; remote-select and upload contracts are dedicated exported contracts; Shell Actions and Shell Overlays are App Shell composition behaviors covered by `erp-shell-actions.spec.ts` and `erp-shell-overlays.spec.ts`, not standalone exported components.

Missing or non-dedicated concepts are: no `ErpActionSecurity` production class (only `erp-action-security.spec.ts` verifies security behavior), no dedicated Entity Rights Workflow symbol, no dedicated Short Header, no dedicated Task Center beyond async/sync action surfaces, and no UI-owned route guard/service layer. Those absences are not automatically defects.

## 5. Current Layer Classification

The **current**, descriptive layering is:

1. `icons`: semantic icon primitive over ng-icons.
2. `essentials`: mixed primitives, action contracts, feedback and overlays.
3. primary/root: compatibility exports plus actions, authorization presentation, navigation, shells and system pages.
4. `forms`: primitives, composite controls and a schema-driven entity form engine.
5. `data-display`: display primitives plus Data Page, Smart Table and filter/tooling compositions.
6. `feedback`: states, dialogs, offline/sync feedback and overlays/facades.
7. `business`: both generic entity page patterns and domain-specific ERP editors.
8. Web core/auth: backend-aware permissions, session, startup, branch, navigation and HTTP policy.
9. Web features: route pages, API adapters, presenters, state/workflow and feature styles.

The labels do not map cleanly to the desired Foundation → Primitives → Composite → Patterns → ERP hierarchy. In particular, `essentials` and root are both foundational and composite; `business` mixes generic Entity Directory/Detail with accounting, stock and payment semantics; and feedback symbols span two entry points.

## 6. Duplicate & Overlap Findings

Nine evidence-backed groups need decisions; “overlap” does not mean automatic merging.

| Group | Evidence | Important difference | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Primary compatibility facades vs secondary APIs | `ui/src/lib/actions/erp-button.ts`, root forms/data/feedback facade files, secondary `public-api.ts` files | Same canonical implementation is exposed through multiple import paths. | **Deprecate candidate**: choose canonical secondary imports; retain timed compatibility facades. |
| Empty/Error states in essentials and feedback | `ui/essentials/src/lib/feedback/erp-empty-state.ts`, `erp-error-state.ts`; `ui/feedback/src/lib/erp-empty-state.ts`, `erp-error-state.ts` | Public symbols/types are duplicated/re-exported; capabilities and ownership are hard to discover. | **Merge/export-surface candidate** after behavioral comparison; one canonical implementation/API. |
| `ErpIcon` vs `HonestyIcon` vocabulary | `ui/icons/src/lib/erp-icon.ts`, primary/essentials public APIs | `HonestyIcon` is a compatibility alias, not an independent renderer. | **Deprecate alias candidate**, keep `ErpIcon`; do not duplicate registries. |
| UI Action Policy vs Web Permission Action Policy | `ui/essentials/.../erp-action-policy.ts`; `web/src/app/authorization/permission-surface.models.ts` | UI describes presentation requirements; Web resolves capability/branch/offline/resource authority. Names overlap, responsibilities legitimately differ. | **Keep both layers**, align terminology and explicit adapter boundary; do not merge into backend-aware UI. |
| UI Unsaved Changes “Guard” vs Web router guard/coordinator | UI action/forms export; `web/src/app/forms/*unsaved*` | UI is confirmation presentation; Web owns routing/form state. | **Rename/deprecate naming candidate** later; keep separation. |
| Sidebar Item/Section vs Navigation Tree | `ui/src/lib/shells/erp-sidebar-item.ts`, `erp-sidebar-section.ts`; `ui/src/lib/navigation/*` | Simple sidebar parts are mainly Showcase/legacy; Navigation Tree owns hierarchical runtime behavior. | **Manual review/internalize candidate**; do not merge solely by name. |
| Entity Actions/output menu vs Print/Export Actions vs Entity Output | `ui/src/lib/actions/erp-entity-actions.ts`; `ui/business/src/lib/erp-entity-output.ts` and print/export files; Web output service | Placement, scope selection, serialization and execution are split across layers. | **Clarify contracts** and one action vocabulary; keep Web execution backend-aware. |
| Canonical feedback vs component-local states | feedback package; `erp-smart-table.ts`, `erp-card-list.ts`, Entity Directory templates | Smart Table/Card List/Directory render overlapping loading/empty/error states with contextual differences. | **Composition candidate**: reuse canonical visuals while retaining contextual orchestration. |
| Generic workflow/commercial bases vs semantic wrappers | `erp-workflow-panels.ts`, `erp-commercial-lines-editor.ts` and maintenance/stock/sale/purchase wrappers | Wrappers constrain business meaning; they are not cosmetic duplicates. | **Keep wrappers**; review whether generic bases should be public or internal. |

No duplicate should be deleted on this audit. The evidence supports public-surface consolidation and internalization more strongly than source-file merging.

## 7. Dependency Boundary Findings

### A. Confirmed violations

1. **ERP business patterns bypass available primitives.** Files including `ui/business/src/lib/erp-commercial-lines-editor.ts`, `erp-journal-lines-editor.ts`, `erp-stock-adjustment-editor.ts`, `erp-report-filter-panel.ts`, workflow panels and permission tree contain direct `<button>`, `<select>` or `<input>` controls. The business package already depends on forms/essentials, so these are higher-layer design-system bypasses, not primitive internals.
2. **Web feature pages bypass the design system.** Static production-template scanning found 32 native buttons in 17 files, 45 selects in 24, 67 inputs in 17, six checkbox inputs in two, three textareas in two, and no native dialogs. Representative concentrations are `web/src/app/maintenance/maintenance-intake/*`, setup-services lists, spare-parts/ink/stabilizers lists, stock-transfer form, and inventory dashboard. Section 21 separates justified internal/print markup from page-level bypasses.

### B. Questionable boundaries requiring decision

- Root/primary UI is imported as a dependency by forms/data/feedback/business yet contains shells and system UI; architecture checks allow this, but the semantic layering is inverted relative to “Foundation”.
- Generic Entity Directory/Detail live under `business` beside accounting and stock editors. Their behavior is generic ERP page-pattern behavior, not domain business behavior.
- `FinancialDataGuard` is a presentational UI gate. Its name can imply enforcement even though actual field/action authority is in Web.
- System pages and sync/offline components are packaged with reusable UI despite being application infrastructure.
- Web customer APIs use generated models/functions plus direct `HttpClient`; this is an application consistency question, not a UI boundary violation.

No UI import of `honesty-api-client`, Web code, `HttpClient`, or backend-specific services was found. No significant circular dependency was confirmed. Architecture checks in `src/frontend/angular/tools` are valuable guardrails.

## 8. Public API Findings

The UI public API is split across seven entry points and exposes approximately 473 unique names: primary 73, business 142, data-display 49, essentials 53, feedback 28, forms 127 and icons 10 before cross-entry de-duplication. This is a large stabilization burden.

Confirmed duplicate public names include `ErpEmptyState`, `ErpEmptyStateSize`, `ErpEmptyStateVariant`, `ErpErrorState`, `ErpIconSource`, `HonestyIcon`, and `HonestyIconName`. The primary API's “narrow” intent is weakened by compatibility re-exports. Conversely, the API client's `public-api.ts` intentionally exposes a broad generated contract surface; that is appropriate for generated code but should not be used as a model for UI stability.

Likely internalization candidates, subject to consumer confirmation, are `ErpSortHeader` (Smart Table implementation), `ErpPageContainer` (Page Shell implementation), generic `ErpWorkflowPanel` and `ErpCommercialLinesEditor` bases when semantic wrappers suffice, and `HonestySystemPageShell`. `ErpEntityReviewTemplate` should remain public if it is the documented template escape hatch.

No significant “implemented and clearly intended for consumers but missing from every public API” case was confirmed. The stronger problem is overexposure and duplicate ownership, not under-exporting. Any future missing-export decision should follow an approved supported-use-case list rather than exporting internals merely because they exist.

The package is **not yet close to an external, versioned API standard**: canonical import paths are ambiguous, advanced implementation contracts are broadly exported, and stability/deprecation markers are absent. Its positive foundation is explicit public-api files, secondary package boundaries, architecture checks, and little accidental relative-path consumption from Web.

## 9. Action Framework

`ErpActionPolicy` in `ui/essentials/src/lib/actions/erp-action-policy.ts` is the reusable presentation-neutral definition. It covers identity, label/icon, tone/variant, required permissions, branch/capability/online requirements, confirmation metadata and busy keys. A feature or application resolver produces availability; UI buttons and menus consume the resolved state rather than querying authority.

`ErpButton` and `ErpIconButton` are renderers. `ErpActionMenu` places multiple actions. `ErpEntityActions` composes page-header action slots and output affordances. `ErpLifecycleActions` represents allowed state transitions. Bulk Action Bar handles selected-row actions. Async locking prevents duplicate client execution; idempotency helpers create keys/reservations but cannot replace server enforcement. `ErpPrintExportActions` and `ErpEntityOutput` add output scope/options and therefore overlap with Entity Actions at placement/model boundaries.

There is no production `ErpActionSecurity` class: `ui/src/lib/actions/erp-action-security.spec.ts` tests security-related expectations. Actual authority resolution is Web-owned through `web/src/app/authorization/permission-policy-engine.service.ts`, `permission-surface.service.ts`, and `permission-surface.models.ts`.

The architecture is moving toward one action-definition vocabulary, but is not unified: UI action requirements, Web permission policies, entity lifecycle actions, bulk actions and output definitions use related but distinct contracts. This is a drift risk, not grounds for putting permission services into UI. Business coupling is acceptably outside Button/Icon Button; the primary concern is contract translation and duplicated placement/output decisions.

## 10. Authorization Architecture

Authorization is correctly split into presentation and enforcement-aware application layers:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C[Generated capabilities/API data] --> E[Web PermissionPolicyEngine]
  B[Active branch/session/offline/resource state] --> E
  E --> S[PermissionSurface / FieldPolicy]
  S --> P[Resolved action/field/navigation state]
  P --> G[UI Permission/Branch/Financial gates]
  P --> A[Action renderers]
  P --> N[Navigation filtering]
```

Evidence in Web: `authorization/permission-policy.models.ts`, `permission-policy-engine.service.ts`, `permission-surface.service.ts`, `field-policy.service.ts`, `permission-route.guard.ts`, and `forbidden-authority.interceptor.ts`. The engine is fail-closed and combines generated capability data with branch, offline, resource and route context. Field policy separately models visibility, editability, exportability and financial sensitivity. Navigation registry filtering prunes inaccessible nodes.

The UI `ErpPermissionGate`, `ErpBranchScopeGate`, and `ErpFinancialDataGuard` only control presentation based on inputs and do not contact a backend. This complies with the desired dependency direction. The caveat is naming: “Guard” can be mistaken for a security boundary. Server authorization remains mandatory and is outside this frontend audit.

## 11. Forms Architecture

### 11.1 End-to-end flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Feature[Feature DTO/domain adapter] --> Schema[Entity Form Schema]
  Schema --> Registry[Entity Field Registry]
  Registry --> Outlet[Schema Fields / dynamic renderer]
  Outlet --> Controls[ERP CVA controls]
  Controls --> RF[Angular Reactive Forms]
  RF --> Validation[Client + Server Validation Mapping]
  RF --> Wizard[Wizard State / Stepper]
  Wizard --> Review[Entity Review]
  Review --> Workflow[Entity Write Workflow]
  Workflow --> FeatureAPI[Web feature API/service]
  Custom[Custom rendererKey/template/component] --> Registry
```

`ErpFormControlBase` implements common ControlValueAccessor mechanics. `ErpFormField` provides label/help/error structure. Primitive controls include text, numeric, password, textarea, date/time/date-time/range, checkbox, radio, switch and selection families. `ErpEntityFormSchema` describes built-in fields, rules and full/half/third layout. `ErpEntityFieldRegistry` and dynamic outlet select renderers by key. Remote select uses a store/request contract with cancellation and stale-result suppression. Repeater and uploads are compositional; file/image upload require adapters rather than HTTP dependencies.

`ErpEntityWizardState`, Stepper, Entity Review, `ErpStandardEntityForm`, and `ErpEntityWriteWorkflow` form a complete conventional entity workflow. Customer create/edit demonstrates this through `web/src/app/features/sales/customers/form/*`: the page delegates to schema, state, workflow, model, adapter and renderer collaborators instead of encoding the entire process in one component.

Answers to the required questions:

1. **Is there a Form Engine?** Yes, effectively: schema + registry/outlet + renderer set + validation + wizard/review/write workflow.
2. **What is schema-driven?** Conventional entity fields, visibility/enablement rules, layout, validation metadata, wizard/review rendering and renderer selection.
3. **Custom escape hatches?** Yes: renderer keys, registry-supplied components/templates, custom sections and feature-owned workflow logic.
4. **Is schema overly complex?** Not yet demonstrably a programming language, but callback-rich customer contexts and 371-line schema-field implementation show pressure. Avoid adding transaction orchestration expressions.
5. **Unnecessary abstractions?** No clear disposable layer; public exposure of base/control internals is broader than necessary.
6. **Business leakage?** Generic forms remain backend-neutral. Customer-specific mapping/rights/workflow stays in Web.
7. **Can complex transactions opt out?** Yes. Journal, commercial, stock and payment editors directly compose reactive forms/controls rather than requiring schema generation.
8. **Validation consistency?** Strong in the customer/standard-form path, including server mapping and summary; older custom pages are inconsistent and often implement local error UX.

The form engine should therefore be preserved and constrained to conventional CRUD, not expanded to absorb every ERP transaction.

## 12. Data Explorer / Smart Table Architecture

`ErpDataSource` contracts define query/result behavior. `ErpDataPage` owns query state, cancellation, retry and page loading without rendering or HTTP knowledge. Feature adapters perform generated/direct API calls and map responses. `ErpSmartTable` renders columns, sorting, row selection, pagination and its loading/empty/error surfaces. Column contracts define value/render behavior; Column Chooser mutates visible-column selection but does not own persistence.

`ErpFilterBar` emits search/filter changes; `ErpFilterDrawer` composes Drawer and form controls. `ErpTableToolbar` is layout/command composition. `ErpViewSwitcher` chooses table/card representation. `ErpCardList` is separate rendering. `ErpEntityDirectory` composes these with KPI, bulk actions, output, footer/context snapshot and feature slots. The feature retains server-side query construction, local persistence, permission resolution and API execution.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Feature[Feature query/API adapter] --> DP[ErpDataPage]
  DP --> Dir[ErpEntityDirectory]
  Dir --> FB[Filter Bar/Drawer]
  Dir --> TT[Table Toolbar]
  Dir --> ST[Smart Table]
  Dir --> CL[Card List]
  Dir --> KPI[KPI Cards]
  ST --> CC[Column contracts/chooser]
  ST --> PG[Pagination]
  Dir --> BA[Bulk/Entity/Output actions]
```

The result is a **coherent Data Explorer pattern**, not one monolithic Smart Table. Smart Table is broad (528 TS lines) but remains a renderer; Entity Directory is the page-level composition (461 TS lines plus template/style) and its runtime is split into ten bounded files. Keep Data Page, Smart Table, filters, pagination, toolbar, chooser, cards and Directory separate. Consolidate visual state rendering and action contracts through composition rather than merging their responsibilities.

Server sorting/filtering/pagination are feature-controlled. Local filtering is possible where a supplied adapter/state chooses it; UI does not assume HTTP. Selection, bulk actions, event outputs and permissions flow through inputs/outputs/resolved actions. Visible-column persistence is feature/application-owned. No backend coupling was found in these UI files.

## 13. Shell & Navigation Architecture

The UI shell family includes App Shell, Auth Shell, System Page Shell, Sidebar, Topbar, Page Shell/Header/Footer, Section Card, Breadcrumbs, Tabs, Branch Selector, User Menu, Notification Bell, Global Search and Theme Toggle. These components are event-driven/content-projected and do not import feature APIs.

The actual authenticated composition lives in `web/src/app/auth/authenticated-workspace/*`, combining UI shell components with Web session, branch, navigation and permission state. Web's navigation registry extends UI nodes with route and permission metadata, filters unavailable branches/items and prunes empty parents. Route activation drives the selected node; expansion state is controlled rather than inferred only from clicks.

Sidebar/navigation characteristics:

- configuration and node contracts live under `ui/src/lib/navigation/*`;
- groups/sections and parent-child nodes are supported;
- a single sibling expansion policy is enforced per level by the state manager;
- active state is synchronized with routes in the Web workspace;
- semantic icon references flow through `ErpIcon`;
- permissions are filtered in Web, not evaluated in UI;
- badges/counts are supported in node configuration;
- navigation state is persisted by `web/src/app/navigation/workspace-navigation.store.ts`, keyed by system/user/branch context;
- the navigation tree validation allows depth up to 12, though the intended normal UX maximum of approximately three levels should remain a content rule;
- responsive/collapsed behavior is shell-controlled and exercised by Showcase viewport tests.

Two systems coexist: simple `ErpSidebarItem`/`ErpSidebarSection`, used mainly in Showcase/legacy-style composition, and the richer Navigation Tree used by the authenticated Web shell. That is a public-surface overlap. There is no dedicated Short Header; `ErpPageHeader` plus Page Shell covers that role. Breadcrumbs are separate and composable.

## 14. Feedback & Overlay Architecture

The feedback package includes Alert, Confirmation Dialog, Concurrency Conflict Dialog, Empty State, Error State, Loading State, Skeleton, Offline Banner, Offline Workspace Banner and Sync Center. Overlay primitives include Drawer, Modal and Tooltip, with compatibility facades in primary/essentials paths.

The strong separation is behavioral: dialogs expose events; Web owns persistence/API decisions. Concurrency conflict presentation is paired with Web row-version/workflow helpers. Offline and sync components display state but do not implement a network queue. Tooltip implements accessible pointer/focus behavior rather than hover-only behavior.

The weakness is canonical state rendering. Smart Table, Card List, Entity Directory and feature pages still contain contextual empty/loading/error renderers in addition to `ErpEmptyState`/`ErpErrorState`. Some context-specific orchestration is necessary, but the visual primitives should be shared. Duplicate essentials/feedback exports obscure the one approved implementation.

## 15. ERP Business Components

The `business` entry point contains two different reuse scopes:

- **Generic ERP page patterns:** Entity Directory, Entity Detail, Attachment List, Audit Timeline, Party contact/address presentations, Entity Output and workflow composition.
- **Domain-specific ERP UI:** Commercial/Sale/Purchase lines, Journal Lines, Payment Allocation, Stock Adjustment, Permission Tree, report filters, maintenance/stock-transfer workflow wrappers.

These should not be described as primitive UI. Their presence is valuable: transaction editors centralize line-level validation, calculation/selection behavior and consistent action layout. The issue is package classification and composition discipline. The largest implementations—Commercial Lines (560 TS lines), Party Address (517), Party Contact (514), Stock Adjustment (384), report filters (367), workflow panels (365), Permission Tree (332) and Journal Lines (323)—deserve focused tests and smaller internal collaborators, but size alone does not make them God Components.

The semantic sale/purchase and maintenance/stock-transfer wrappers are useful because they prevent consumers from configuring an unconstrained universal component. The generic bases may be internal candidates. Direct native controls inside these high-level components are a confirmed design-system boundary problem, even though their business logic belongs here.

## 16. Application/System Infrastructure

Web, not UI, owns backend/session/runtime concerns. Important areas include:

- startup orchestration and probes under `web/src/app/startup/*`;
- authenticated session and expiry/multi-tab behavior under `web/src/app/auth/*`;
- active branch context in `web/src/app/auth/active-branch-context.service.ts`;
- HTTP interceptors that attach authentication and `X-Current-Branch-Id`, handle forbidden authority and session failures;
- permission route/field/action infrastructure under `web/src/app/authorization/*`;
- Web form unsaved-change coordination/route guard under `web/src/app/forms/*`;
- feature API adapters, generated-contract mapping, output execution and row-version concurrency handling.

UI system pages—Backend Unavailable, Forbidden, Initialization Required and Session Expiry—are presentation endpoints for that orchestration. Startup/session/branch architecture is a strong part of the codebase and directly addresses the earlier class of lost-branch/session failures.

Sync Center exists as a presentational UI surface, but the current authenticated shell initializes an empty sync-item signal; no complete generic offline queue was proven by this audit. No dedicated Task UI/Task Center was found beyond async action and sync feedback. Those are “not proven implemented”, not dead-code conclusions.

## 17. SCSS & Theme Architecture

### 17.1 Observed organization

`ui/src/styles/_index.scss` is the shared entry. `_tokens.scss`, `_themes.scss`, foundation/global rules and entity styles feed component-local SCSS. Components generally use BEM-like class names, CSS custom properties and logical properties (`inset-inline-*`, `margin-inline-*`, etc.), which is positive for RTL. Light/dark selection is CSS-variable based rather than separate component implementations.

### 17.2 Quantitative evidence

Static scanning across 424 production UI/Web style-bearing files produced:

| Measure | Count | Interpretation |
|---|---:|---|
| Hex color occurrences | 493 | Too many values bypass semantic color tokens or duplicate fallback literals. |
| `rgb()`/`rgba()` occurrences | 49 | Additional local color/shadow behavior. |
| `!important` occurrences | 26 | Some are legitimate reduced-motion overrides; others are component/page hacks. |
| `rem` occurrences | 1,957 | Unit choice is generally scalable, but values are not governed by a complete spacing/type scale. |
| `px` occurrences | 984 | Includes borders/icons/layout constraints; needs category-specific review, not blanket removal. |
| Distinct media-query breakpoints | 39 | Strong evidence of breakpoint fragmentation. |
| Central token definitions in `_tokens.scss` | about 48 | A foundation exists but is incomplete. |
| Referenced `--honesty-*` names absent from central token file | 32 | May be locally/theme-defined, but canonical ownership is missing. |

Frequently repeated breakpoints include `48rem` (18 occurrences), `40rem` (17), `64rem` (10), `30rem` (9), `42rem`/`35rem` (8 each), `36rem` (7), and `32rem` (6). This is not a coherent named breakpoint map.

The 32 variables not declared in the central token file include families such as `--honesty-color-app-bg`, `border-subtle`, `danger-subtle`, `primary-soft`/`primary-subtle`, `surface-hover`, `text-primary`/`secondary`/`subtle`, font mono/size/weight/line-height variables, `motion-normal`, `radius-full`/`pill`/`xl`, shadow levels, higher spacing names, direction factor and dropdown z-index. “Not central” does not mean undefined at runtime; it means the design system lacks one authoritative contract.

### 17.3 System coverage

- **Color:** semantic color variables exist, but component/page literals remain common.
- **Typography:** font loading/family exists, yet central size/weight/line-height scales are incomplete and local typography is widespread.
- **Spacing/radius:** token names exist, but missing central levels and arbitrary local values weaken rhythm.
- **Borders/shadows:** repeated local combinations and incomplete elevation tokens cause inconsistent cards/overlays.
- **Icons/control heights/table density:** semantic icon sizing and variants exist in components, but there is no single comprehensive scale for icon/control/table density.
- **Z-index/motion:** individual behavior exists; a complete layer/motion contract is not evident.
- **RTL:** logical properties are common and Arabic-first templates are strong; remaining physical left/right rules require targeted review.
- **Themes:** light/dark files exist, but the dark theme redefines more variables than light and Web global styles include a hard-coded body background `#f3f3f9`, so theme parity is not guaranteed.

The most important issue is not any single value; it is that components can bypass the central visual contract without governance. Configuration should stay semantic—variant, size, density, state—not expose arbitrary padding, radius, color or font values per page.

## 18. Visual Consistency Findings

### 18.1 What was actually visually inspectable

Reliable fresh rendering was **not possible** in the audit constraints. The Showcase serve process failed at TypeScript resolution because built UI entry points were absent. Building would create repository artifacts beyond the permitted report, so no workaround was performed.

Committed Playwright image baselines under `src/frontend/angular/e2e-showcase` provide limited rendered evidence for checkbox, radio, select, tooltip, empty state, KPI card and customer-360 reference surfaces, in dark-oriented 1440×1000 captures dated in the repository. They prove deliberate visual targets and regression intent, but not that the present source still renders identically.

### 18.2 Confirmed from committed rendered baselines

- Checkbox, radio, advanced select, tooltip, empty state, KPI and customer-360 each have concrete reference images rather than prose-only specifications.
- The intended components use a cohesive dark palette, semantic focus/accent treatment, controlled rounding and Arabic/RTL layouts.
- Dedicated templates are substantially richer than a native control: select demonstrates search/filter/group/multi/chips/avatar/clear behavior; empty state includes illustration/action/help; KPI includes semantic tone, comparison and metadata.

### 18.3 Inferred from source and style evidence

- Sidebar/topbar/page shell proportions are controlled by multiple local SCSS files rather than a fully centralized shell-density contract.
- Typography hierarchy, card radius/shadows, content spacing, button/control heights, filter rhythm and table density can diverge because central scales are incomplete.
- Native controls in business/Web pages cannot reliably match ERP controls across themes, focus, disabled and RTL states.
- Smart Table/Card List/Directory local states may visually diverge from canonical Empty/Error/Loading components.
- Dark/light parity is at risk from asymmetric theme definitions and hard-coded Web colors.
- Thirty-nine breakpoints make responsive behavior difficult to reason about, even with desktop-first intent.

These are implementation-level consistency findings, not claims that every rendered screen is visibly broken. A later visual audit should run both applications, capture the same routes in light/dark and target desktop widths, then compare against the approved references.

## 19. UI Showcase Coverage

The Showcase is a real catalog application, not a single demo page. Its sections/playgrounds include showcase shell/app, Button, Icon, entity layout, navigation, data display, business, feedback, form, entity schema form, overlay and security. The catalog reports 31 ready entries. `e2e-showcase/showcase.spec.ts` exercises mobile/tablet/desktop viewports, table selection/card view/offline/error behavior, business interactions, theme/direction/state controls, action menus/bulk actions, overlays and lifecycle actions.

Quality tests include viewports 360×800, 390×844, 768×1024, 1024×768, 1366×768 and 1920×1080; Axe checks target WCAG 2.2 AA for ten sections in both themes; focus and reduced-motion cases also exist. This makes Showcase useful for safe visual change, once clean-checkout startup is repaired.

| Component/Pattern | Showcase Exists | Main States Covered | Dark | Light | RTL | Missing Cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Button/Icon Button | Yes | variants, disabled/loading, actions | Yes | Yes | Yes | Cross-browser visual baselines. |
| Action Menu/Bulk/Lifecycle | Yes | menu, selection, lifecycle interactions | Yes | Yes | Yes | Full Web permission integration. |
| Icons | Yes | semantic catalog (~46 registered icons) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Missing-icon/fallback documentation. |
| Checkbox/Radio/Switch | Yes | size/variant/disabled/selection | Yes | Yes | Yes | More validation combinations. |
| Select/Multi/Remote Select | Yes | open/search/filter/group/chips | Yes | Yes | Yes | Network latency/auth failure matrix. |
