The major operational gap is that direct `start:ui-showcase:serve` is not self-sufficient in a clean workspace with absent UI `dist`; dependency-aware scripts exist, but the simplest documented/start target is brittle. No packages or configuration were changed during this audit.

## 20. Web Usage Findings

Web imports generated API contracts/functions/services in approximately 144 source files and consumes UI through package entry points. Direct `HttpClient` appears in a much smaller set: application config/infrastructure, active-branch context, startup probe, customers, roles, users and wallets APIs. This indicates generated-client adoption with a few explicit adapters, not UI/backend coupling.

| Representative screen | UI composition | Feature logic/adaptation | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer list | `ErpPageShell` + `ErpEntityDirectory` + footer + confirmations | `features/sales/customers/list` page (294 TS lines), presenter (357), state (125), loader (74), bulk actions (247), policy (198), output (50) | Best current page-pattern example; no native controls in the feature. |
| Customer create/edit | Page Shell + Standard Entity Form + Stepper + Form Section + Schema Fields + Review + confirm/concurrency | form page (357), state (399), workflow (464), models (320), schema (257), adapter/renderers | Strong separation and custom escape hatches; callback/context complexity should be watched. |
| Customer detail | Page Shell + Entity Detail + footer + confirmations | detail page (235), actions (267), presenter (290), state (185), schema (365), adapter/renderers | Strong registry/action composition; feature mapping stays outside UI. |
| Supplier list/form/detail | Mixed UI components and feature-local markup/styles | list 1,276 TS; form 1,327; detail 1,044 | Pre-golden-standard architecture; large page classes repeat UX/orchestration. |
| Maintenance detail/intake | Mixed shell/forms plus native controls and local state | detail 1,374 TS; intake has highest native-control concentration | High refactoring candidate after customer standard is frozen. |
| Shipping list/detail/form | Feature-specific pages and repeated list/form/detail behavior | 1,295/1,292/1,267 TS respectively | Strong evidence of duplicated feature orchestration. |
| Inventory/dashboard and stock transfer | UI pieces plus custom dashboard/transaction composition | inventory dashboard 1,034 TS; stock-transfer form contains native inputs | Complex screens should compose ERP editors, not be forced into entity schema. |
| Reports | Report Filter Panel and feature-owned API/query mapping where adopted | generated API models mapped in Web | Correct desired direction; adoption is uneven. |

Other very large pages include employee detail (1,962 TS), spare-parts list (1,197), devices list (1,174), category detail (1,122), ink list (1,093), stabilizers list (1,085), and setup-services list (1,027). Line count is not a defect by itself, but together with native controls and mixed API/state/view logic it identifies concrete God-page risk.

Routes in `web/src/app/app.routes.ts` and feature route files expose sales/customers, purchases/suppliers, logistics/shipping, catalog, inventory, maintenance, finance/wallets, HR and administration. A route catalog retains old `/workspace/*` mappings to canonical modular routes; evidence suggests intentional compatibility, not unreachable legacy.

### Current architecture as implemented

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  OpenAPI[OpenAPI-generated API Client] --> Adapters[Web feature APIs/adapters]
  Runtime[Web startup/session/branch/permission] --> Features[Web feature pages]
  Adapters --> Features
  UIPrim[UI essentials/icons/forms/data/feedback] --> UIPatterns[UI root + business patterns]
  UIPatterns --> Features
  UIPrim --> Showcase[UI Showcase]
  UIPatterns --> Showcase
  Features --> Modern[Decomposed features: Customers]
  Features --> Legacy[Large page-centric features]
```

This is the current reality: one generated backend package, one broad multi-entry UI package, two applications, backend-aware infrastructure in Web, and mixed generations of feature implementation. It is not yet the recommended target layering in section 25.

## 21. Design-System Bypass Findings

Static production Web template scanning found:

| Native element | Count | Files | Assessment |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `<button>` | 32 | 17 | Mostly feature-level bypass; primitive internals excluded from this Web count. |
| `<select>` | 45 | 24 | Strongest repeated bypass of `ErpSelect`. |
| `<input>` | 67 | 17 | Includes text/date/checkbox; requires per-use migration decision. |
| checkbox inputs | 6 | 2 | One employee form and five maintenance-intake uses. |
| radio inputs | 0 | 0 | No Web production bypass found. |
| `<textarea>` | 3 | 2 | Feature-local bypass. |
| `<table>` | 3 | 3 | All occur in generated print HTML strings; intentional, not live design-system bypass. |
| native `<dialog>` | 0 | 0 | Overlay components are being used. |

Representative high concentrations are maintenance intake (15 native controls), setup-services list (13), spare-parts list (12), ink list (10), stabilizers list (9), bootstrap setup (9), maintenance setup/work (8), stock-transfer form (6), and inventory dashboard (6). Customer list/form/detail contain no direct native controls, showing the target composition is achievable.

The UI business package itself contains 26 direct buttons, six selects and 17 inputs. Native elements inside primitive components such as `ErpButton`, `ErpSelect` and Checkbox are correct implementation details; native elements inside Commercial/Journal/Stock/Report/Workflow/Permission patterns are boundary bypasses because those components can consume established primitives.

## 22. Dead / Legacy Code Candidates

### Confirmed unused

None. Static repository search cannot prove a public package symbol is unused by external consumers, and no deletion recommendation is justified.

### Potentially unused

- `ErpFinancialDataGuard` (`ui/src/lib/authorization/...`): exported, but no direct Web/Showcase consumer was found.
- `ErpInitializationRequiredPage` (`ui/src/lib/system/...`): exported, but no direct Web/Showcase consumer was found.

### Exported but apparently internal

Consumer scans found no direct Web/Showcase use for `ErpSortHeader`, `ErpPageContainer`, generic Commercial Lines/Workflow bases, and `HonestySystemPageShell`, while their higher-level parents/wrappers use them. They are **internalization candidates**, not dead code. `ErpEntityReviewTemplate` also lacks a direct current consumer but is a legitimate extension contract and should not be called dead.

Simple Sidebar Item/Section and multiple root compatibility facades look like an older API shape beside Navigation Tree/secondary entry points. Review them through deprecation telemetry or a full import graph before removal.

Potential package dependency residue—no non-test source imports found—includes `@ng-bootstrap/ng-bootstrap`, `@ngrx/store`, `@ngx-translate/core`, `angularx-flatpickr`, `@lordicon/element`, `simplebar-angular`, `sweetalert2`, `ngx-cookie-service`, `ngx-csv` and `lottie-web`. Build tooling, side effects or future integration may still justify them; this audit does not authorize removal.

## 23. Strong Existing Architecture Worth Preserving

- **UI/backend independence:** no UI import of API client, HTTP or Web services.
- **Semantic icon façade:** `ErpIcon` hides ng-icons/vendor packs, supports tree shaking and lets applications use semantic references.
- **Permission split:** Web resolves authority; UI gates/actions render resolved state. Field-level policy is explicitly modeled.
- **Generated API boundary:** generated contracts remain in a dedicated project; feature adapters map into UI configurations.
- **Data contracts and cancellation:** Data Page/remote selection prevent stale requests without knowing backend URLs.
- **Composable Data Explorer:** Smart Table, filters, toolbar, cards, pagination and Directory remain separable.
- **Form registry escape hatch:** conventional CRUD is schema-driven while custom renderers and transaction editors can opt out.
- **Customer decomposition:** list/form/detail pages delegate to presenters, state, workflows, schemas, adapters and policies.
- **Entity Detail section registry:** allows feature sections without making one universal detail component.
- **Navigation policy/persistence:** permissions are pruned in Web and state is keyed to session/branch context.
- **Startup/session/branch handling:** orchestration and interceptors centralize cross-cutting context rather than duplicating it per feature.
- **Concurrency and output boundaries:** reusable UI dialogs/contracts are separated from Web row-version/API/output execution.
- **Governance and tests:** architecture checks, icon registry checks, Showcase Playwright, Axe, viewport and baseline tests are meaningful assets.

These capabilities should survive visual redesign and package reclassification. The correct strategy is controlled convergence, not replacement.

## 24. Technical Risks

### Critical

None proven by this audit. The failed direct Showcase start is a clean-workspace/tooling defect, but a dependency-aware build route exists and production runtime failure was not established.

### High — six areas

1. **Clean-checkout validation is brittle.** `src/frontend/angular/tsconfig.json` points package aliases to `dist`; `start:ui-showcase:serve` failed when those packages were absent. This can prevent the visual safety net from running at exactly the moment it is needed.
2. **Public API instability and ambiguity.** Approximately 473 unique exports, duplicate symbols across primary/essentials/feedback/icons, and compatibility facades make canonical imports/versioning unclear. Evidence: all seven UI `public-api.ts` files.
3. **Theme/token fragmentation.** 493 hex occurrences, 39 breakpoints, 32 non-central token names and hard-coded Web canvas color undermine consistent light/dark/RTL redesign. Evidence: `ui/src/styles/*`, component SCSS and `web/src/styles.scss`.
4. **Parallel feature architectures.** Golden-standard customers are decomposed, while employee/supplier/shipping/maintenance/inventory pages reach 1,000–1,962 TS lines. This multiplies UX logic and raises change cost.
5. **Primitive bypass at two layers.** UI business patterns and Web features contain direct buttons/selects/inputs despite established primitives, causing accessibility/theme/RTL drift. Evidence and counts are in sections 7 and 21.
6. **Action/output policy drift.** UI Action Policy, Web Permission Action Policy, lifecycle/bulk/entity actions and output models overlap without one explicit adaptation contract. Evidence: `ui/**/erp-action-policy.ts`, `ui/src/lib/actions/*`, `ui/business/.../erp-entity-output.ts`, and `web/src/app/authorization/*`.

### Medium

- Form schema complexity may expand beyond CRUD if transaction behavior is added to it.
- Smart Table and Entity Directory are sizeable coordination points; visual states already overlap canonical feedback.
- `business` combines generic patterns and domain-specific ERP editors, increasing accidental coupling.
- Navigation has two component families and technically permits depth 12 despite a three-level UX guideline.
- Sync/offline UI appears more mature than proven application queue behavior.
- Potential dependency residue increases maintenance/security surface until verified.

### Low

- Compatibility naming (`HonestyIcon`, UI “Guard”) reduces clarity.
- Missing dedicated showcases for a few system/financial states reduce confidence but not runtime correctness.
- Some `!important` and physical-direction rules need review; several are legitimate accessibility resets.

## 25. Recommended Target Layering

This is classification guidance only; no files should move until public API and migration decisions are approved.

| Target layer | Existing examples | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Foundation | tokens, themes, typography, spacing, motion, breakpoints, direction utilities, icon contracts | One authoritative visual/runtime vocabulary; no Angular business behavior. |
| Primitives | Button, Icon Button, Icon, form controls, Status Badge, basic layout/text display | Small semantic controls with fixed design-system choices. |
| Forms | Form Field, validators, CVA base, select/upload/repeater, server-error mapping | Cohesive form behavior without entity/business semantics. |
| Data | Money/date display, columns, Data Page, Table, pagination, chooser, card list | Backend-neutral data state and display. |
| Feedback | Alert, Empty/Error/Loading/Skeleton, confirmation/concurrency visuals | Canonical state visuals and user response. |
| Overlays | Drawer, Modal, Tooltip and focus/stack infrastructure | Reusable interaction layer shared by forms/shell/patterns. |
| Navigation | navigation contracts/tree and route-independent state | Hierarchical navigation behavior, independent of feature registry. |
| Composite Components | Filter Drawer, Table Toolbar, Branch Selector, user/notification menus | Multi-primitive assemblies with focused responsibility. |
| Generic UI Patterns | Standard Entity Form, Smart data exploration composition, form wizard/review | Repeated UX logic without ERP-specific DTOs. |
| Shell | App/Auth/System/Page shells, topbar/sidebar/header/footer/breadcrumbs/tabs | Stable application framing, no feature modules. |
| ERP Business UI | Entity Directory/Detail/Output, party, journal, commercial, stock, payment, workflow editors | Reusable ERP semantics; may compose all lower layers. |
| Application/System Infrastructure | permission engine, startup/session/branch, route guards, HTTP, sync orchestration | Backend/environment-aware behavior belongs in Web or a dedicated application package. |
| Features | customers, suppliers, maintenance, finance, inventory, etc. | DTO mapping, API execution, domain workflows and route pages. |

The key split is reuse scope: Button/Select/Modal are universal UI; Entity Directory/Form are generic product patterns; Journal/Payment/Stock editors are ERP business UI; startup/permissions/API execution are application infrastructure. Public entry points should mirror this dependency direction rather than historical folders.

## 26. Open Questions Requiring Human Decision

1. Which secondary entry point is canonical for Empty/Error/Loading and overlays, and how long must root/essentials compatibility imports live?
2. Should generic Entity Directory/Detail and Standard Entity Form be called generic patterns or explicitly ERP patterns?
3. Are generic Commercial Lines and Workflow bases intended for third-party consumers, or should only semantic wrappers be public?
4. Should UI `ErpActionPolicy` and Web `ActionPolicy` keep the same word with qualified names, or use explicit “requirement” versus “resolved permission” terminology?
5. Is visible-column/filter/view persistence a feature responsibility or a shared application persistence service?
6. Is three navigation levels a validation rule or only a content-design guideline? The current tree accepts up to 12.
7. Which current light/dark visual references are approved as targets? Existing committed baselines should not silently define the redesign.
8. What is the browser/desktop-width support matrix, including minimum supported width, high zoom and reduced motion?
9. Is offline/sync an actual roadmap capability requiring durable queue/conflict behavior, or only connection-state feedback?
10. Which potentially unused dependencies are build-time/side-effect requirements versus legacy residue?
11. Are direct `HttpClient` feature adapters intentional exceptions to generated clients, and what contract governs them?
12. What deprecation/versioning policy will apply when the UI package is treated as an external stable package?

## 27. Suggested Next Audit/Refactoring Sequence

This sequence deliberately separates decisions from implementation and keeps Customers as the golden standard.

1. **Freeze evidence and repair auditability:** decide the clean-checkout build/serve contract; run architecture checks, unit tests, Showcase E2E and visual captures without manual prerequisite ambiguity.
2. **Approve boundaries and canonical imports:** decide target layers, canonical entry points, public/internal symbols and deprecation policy. Produce an import migration map before moving anything.
3. **Token/theme specification audit:** inventory approved colors/type/spacing/radius/elevation/control/density/motion/breakpoints and compare rendered light/dark RTL states to references. This precedes visual component rewrites.
4. **Primitive fidelity audit:** validate Icon, Button/Icon Button, Checkbox/Radio/Switch, Select family, Tooltip, overlays and state components against approved references, accessibility and keyboard behavior.
5. **Canonical feedback/action contracts:** settle Empty/Error/Loading ownership and define the adapter between UI action requirements, Web authority and output/lifecycle/bulk placements.
6. **Revalidate Customers end to end:** list, filter, pagination, cards/table, KPI, empty/error/loading, create/edit wizard, server validation, unsaved changes, detail sections, output, lifecycle, field/action permissions, concurrency and branch/session recovery.
7. **Extract a written feature adoption contract:** document exactly what another entity reuses, which feature collaborators are required, where custom renderers belong and what must never be duplicated.
8. **Pilot one representative non-customer feature:** choose one ordinary CRUD entity, measure deleted duplicated UX logic, and refine the contract without changing all features at once.
9. **Pilot one complex transaction separately:** validate that Journal/Commercial/Stock/Payment patterns compose primitives and can opt out of schema generation cleanly.
10. **Migrate by bounded feature slices:** suppliers/maintenance/etc. only after the customer and pilot contracts are stable; maintain independent verification gates.
11. **Retire compatibility/legacy surfaces:** only after import telemetry/search proves no consumers; deprecate first, then remove in a versioned change.
12. **Dependency and dead-code cleanup:** verify package/build/side-effect use before removal; do not combine cleanup with architectural moves.

## Decision rules used

- **Preserve logic / redesign visual**: behavior is reusable and tested, but current visuals are not an approved target.
- **Refine API**: canonical high-reuse patterns whose public contracts need stabilization or clearer layer ownership.
- **Compose from existing primitives**: high-layer components containing confirmed native-control bypasses.
- **Internalize**: exported implementation/base helpers without a demonstrated direct application contract.
- **Manual design decision**: repository evidence cannot establish removal/replacement safely.

No row authorizes implementation, relocation, removal, or baseline updates.

# ERP Visual Audit

> Visual judgements are grounded in the fresh screenshots indexed by `ERP_VISUAL_EVIDENCE_INDEX.md`. **OBSERVED** denotes rendered evidence. **STATIC EVIDENCE** denotes templates/SCSS/tokens. **HUMAN DESIGN DECISION** identifies aesthetic choices that repository evidence cannot settle.

## 1. Reliability and scope

Both runnable applications were served after correcting their development alias paths. Browser capture produced 56 fresh screenshots across Light/Dark RTL scenarios. Runtime capture found no console warnings/errors, page errors, failed requests or HTTP failures in those scripted scenarios. Existing Web E2E reached 166/166 after a semantic pointer-target correction. The audit therefore had reliable rendered evidence for Showcase families and the customer golden feature. It did not claim equivalent visual coverage for every one of the 63 page components.

## 2. Global visual coherence

- **OBSERVED:** Light and Dark use the same structural system and remain recognizably the same product. Evidence: [Showcase foundation light](audit-artifacts/visual/showcase/catalog/foundation-1440x900-light.png), [dark](audit-artifacts/visual/showcase/catalog/foundation-1440x900-dark.png), [Customer list light](audit-artifacts/visual/web/customer/list-1440x900-light.png), [dark](audit-artifacts/visual/web/customer/list-1440x900-dark.png).
- **OBSERVED:** Typography, surfaces and indigo action color are broadly coherent inside the modern Customer pages.
- **OBSERVED:** Catalog and data pages become extremely tall; dense reference content is organized, but the vertical scanning cost is high. Evidence: forms/data catalog screenshots and Customer table/card captures.
- **STATIC EVIDENCE:** 102 distinct literal colors, 39 distinct radius values, 17 distinct z-index values, 173 media queries and 27 `!important` occurrences across 191 style-bearing production/Showcase sources show that coherence is not yet enforced by a compact token vocabulary.

## 3. Shell and navigation

- **OBSERVED:** At 1440/1920, Sidebar, Topbar and content area have a stable relationship; active navigation and hierarchy are readable.
- **OBSERVED:** At 1024 the full-width sidebar still consumes a substantial portion of the viewport and compresses page content. Evidence: [Showcase 1024 dark](audit-artifacts/visual/showcase/viewport/landing-1024x768-dark.png), [Web list 1024 dark](audit-artifacts/visual/web/customer/list-1024x768-dark.png).
- **OBSERVED:** Topbar contains several competing controls and labels; this is dense but technically aligned. Whether to reduce it is a **HUMAN DESIGN DECISION**.
- **STATIC EVIDENCE:** `ErpAppShell` changes to overlay navigation only below 61.99rem; 1024px remains in the desktop fixed-sidebar regime.

## 4. Page framing and headers

- **OBSERVED:** Page Header, KPIs and Directory form a consistent stack on Customer list pages.
- **OBSERVED:** Breadcrumb and header occupy separate vertical bands; the proposal to integrate them is a design decision, not an architectural necessity.
- **OBSERVED:** Customer create/edit retains action affordances in header/form regions, which increases visual competition; behavior is consistent but placement should be standardized during redesign.

## 5. Controls

- **OBSERVED:** Select open states provide search, grouping, filters, icons/avatars, selection and clear affordances in both themes. Evidence: [Select Light](audit-artifacts/visual/showcase/interaction/select-open-light.png), [Select Dark](audit-artifacts/visual/showcase/interaction/select-open-dark.png).
- **OBSERVED:** Checkbox/radio visuals remained unchanged after correcting the native hit target; full Web E2E proves interaction correctness.
- **OBSERVED:** Native browser date placeholders remain `mm/dd/yyyy` in an Arabic drawer. Evidence: [Customer filter drawer](audit-artifacts/visual/web/interaction/customer-filter-drawer-light.png). This is a visible localization inconsistency.
- **OBSERVED/TEST:** Axe found unnamed select fields in Smart Table/page-size and complex/contact examples, plus undersized Select clear targets. This is interaction semantics/target correctness, not a broad compliance claim.

## 6. Data, KPI and directory

- **OBSERVED:** KPI cards share hierarchy, icon placement and theme treatment across Showcase and Customer Web; values load coherently in the fixture.
- **OBSERVED:** Customer table at 1024 visibly clips/truncates the far-left date column. Evidence: [Customer list 1024 dark](audit-artifacts/visual/web/customer/list-1024x768-dark.png). This is an objective desktop-width layout problem.
- **OBSERVED:** Table and card views both render 25 fixture items, producing very long pages; the pattern works but density/pagination placement needs a human product decision.
- **OBSERVED:** Card view ends with an incomplete row; technically valid, visually unbalanced. Evidence: customer-card-view Light/Dark.

## 7. Entity detail and forms

- **OBSERVED:** Entity Detail at 1440 leaves a large unused lower rail/column while central fields wrap; email/name values wrap earlier than expected. Evidence: [Detail 1440 dark](audit-artifacts/visual/web/customer/detail-1440x900-dark.png).
- **OBSERVED:** At 1024 the layout remains usable but compressed; large blank vertical space persists. Evidence: detail 1024 Light/Dark.
- **OBSERVED:** Customer create/edit wizard structure is coherent and clear, but low-contrast field surfaces and long vertical whitespace reduce information density. Evidence: create/edit 1440 Light/Dark.
- **HUMAN DESIGN DECISION:** Exact card radius, elevation and density should be resolved through token redesign, not per-page overrides.

## 8. Feedback and overlays

- **OBSERVED:** Modal has a clear centered surface and backdrop in both themes. Evidence: modal-open Light/Dark.
- **OBSERVED:** Drawer has a clear hierarchy and stable width; Web filter drawer appears on the physical left in RTL. Whether it should use start/end is a documented UX decision.
- **OBSERVED:** Tooltip renders in hover state in both themes; keyboard correctness is additionally covered by source/test behavior.
- **STATIC EVIDENCE:** Multiple contextual empty/loading/error renderers coexist with canonical feedback components, risking visual drift.

## 9. Theme and RTL

- **OBSERVED:** No broad Light/Dark component inversion or missing-theme surface was found in captured scenarios.
- **OBSERVED:** RTL alignment is consistent in all fresh captures; long Arabic labels and numeric values remain readable in primary scenarios.
- **STATIC EVIDENCE:** Physical directions and numerous component-local literal colors still require a dedicated token/RTL cleanup before visual redesign can be called systemic.

## 10. Regression and blockers

- Showcase E2E: **22 passed / 1 failed**. Customer-360 baseline expected 1060×1073 and actual is 1060×1072; diff also contains distributed text/icon pixels. Baseline was intentionally preserved.
- Showcase quality: **13 passed / 1 failed**. Axe failure details are preserved under `audit-artifacts/data/showcase-quality-failure/`.
- Web E2E after repair: **166 passed / 0 failed**.

## 11. Redesign conclusion

The logic of Shell, Select family, Data Page, Entity Directory, Standard Entity Form, Entity Detail, feedback and overlay primitives is strong enough to preserve. Their SCSS/token expression should be redesigned in a controlled order. The 1024 table clipping, detail-space imbalance, localized date presentation, token fragmentation and failing Showcase quality/regression gates must be resolved before using the current visuals as a gold baseline.

## النتيجة التنفيذية

- تم اكتشاف **4 مشاريع Angular**.
- الإصدار الفعلي هو **Angular 21.2.4**، وليس Angular 22.
- نجح بناء:
  - API Client.
  - UI Library بكل مداخلها العامة السبعة.
  - UI Showcase.
  - Web.
- تم تشغيل Showcase وWeb فعلياً، وكلاهما يستجيب الآن بحالة HTTP 200.
- نجحت اختبارات الوحدة والمكوّنات بالكامل: **1,157 من 1,157**.
- نجحت اختبارات Web E2E بالكامل بعد الإصلاحات الدنيا: **166 من 166**.
- نجحت جميع فحوصات المعمارية والحوكمة والأيقونات وتوليد الـAPI وحدود الكيانات وصفحات العملاء.
- تم التقاط **56 صورة Runtime جديدة**، بالإضافة إلى صورتين جديدتين لإثبات اختلاف الـVisual Regression: Actual وDiff.
- لم تُسجّل في سيناريوهات الالتقاط أي:
  - Browser console errors.
  - Browser console warnings.
  - Page errors.
  - Failed requests.
  - HTTP responses بحالة 400 أو أعلى.
- تم الحفاظ على حالات الفشل الحقيقية وعدم التلاعب بها:
  - Showcase E2E: **22 ناجح، 1 فاشل** بسبب اختلاف بصري حقيقي.
  - Showcase Quality: **13 ناجح، 1 فاشل** بسبب مشكلات أسماء حقول Select وحجم أهداف أزرار المسح.
  - لم يتم تحديث صور الأساس لإجبار الاختبار على النجاح.
  - لم يتم تعطيل أو تخفيف فحص Axe.

## أهم الحقائق المعمارية

- UI لا تستورد API Client أو Web أو `HttpClient` أو خدمات الباك إند.
- يوجد **532 صف تصدير عام عبر المداخل السبعة**، تمثل **525 رمزاً Canonical** بعد إزالة التكرار الناتج عن إعادة التصدير.
- التوزيع الدقيق:
  - 115 Component.
  - 5 Directives.
  - 0 Pipes.
  - 0 Injectable Services مصدّرة من UI.
  - 6 State classes.
  - 1 Store.
  - 1 Guard.
  - 183 Interface/Contract.
  - 159 Type aliases.
- يوجد **125 Route record**، منها:
  - 80 مساراً يعرض صفحات.
  - 63 Page Components فريدة.
  - 10 Page Archetypes.
- توجد **9 مجموعات تداخل أو ازدواج مفاهيمي**.
- توجد **مخالفتان معماريتان رئيسيتان مؤكّدتان**:
  1. مكوّنات ERP Business تستخدم native controls بدلاً من تركيب الـprimitives الموجودة.
  2. عدد كبير من صفحات Web القديمة يتجاوز Design System ويقرر UX الخاص به محلياً.
- العملاء هم أفضل نموذج معماري حالي، لكنهم لم يصبحوا بعد مرجعاً بصرياً نهائياً بسبب مشاكل العرض التي كشفها التدقيق.
- عدد من الصفحات القديمة ما زال Page-centric وGod Class:
  - Employee Detail: 1,963 سطراً.
  - Maintenance Detail: 1,375.
  - Supplier Form: 1,328.
  - Shipping List: 1,296.
  - Shipping Detail: 1,293.
  - Suppliers List: 1,277.
  - Shipping Form: 1,268.
- صفحة العملاء نفسها أصبحت موزعة إلى Page/State/Workflow/Presenter/Schema/Adapter، ولم تعد God Class واحدة كما كانت سابقاً.

## تجاوزات Design System

العدّ الآلي في Web:

- `<button>`: 32.
- `<select>`: 45.
- Non-checkbox `<input>`: 35.
- Checkbox: 32.
- Radio: 0.
- `<textarea>`: 3.
- Native dialogs: 0.

وفي طبقة UI Business:

- Buttons: 88.
- Selects: 7.
- Non-checkbox inputs: 27.
- Checkboxes: 2.

يجب عدم تفسير native elements داخل `ErpButton` أو `ErpSelect` أو بقية primitives كمخالفة؛ الجرد يفصل بين التطبيق الصحيح داخل primitive وبين استخدامها مباشرة داخل طبقات Business/Web الأعلى.

## النتائج المرئية المؤكدة

- جدول العملاء يُظهر قصاً/ضغطاً واضحاً للعمود الأيسر عند عرض 1024px.
- تخطيط تفاصيل العميل يهدر مساحة كبيرة في العمود/الشريط الجانبي، في الوقت الذي تلتف فيه قيم الوسط مبكراً.
- Native date input يعرض `mm/dd/yyyy` داخل واجهة عربية.
- صفحات الجدول والكروت تصبح طويلة جداً عند عرض 25 عنصراً.
- Card View ينتهي بصف غير مكتمل بصرياً.
- الـSelect المتقدم يعمل ويعرض البحث والتجميع والأيقونات والصور والـchips في Light/Dark، لكن توجد حقول Select تفتقد أسماءً تشغيلية صحيحة.
- زرا المسح في مثالين للـSelect أصغر من الحد الذي يفحصه اختبار Target Size.
- يوجد اختلاف حقيقي بين Customer-360 الحالي وصورة الأساس؛ الفرق ليس مجرد بكسل واحد في الارتفاع، بل توجد فروق موزعة في النصوص والأيقونات أيضاً.
- Light/Dark وRTL متسقة بصورة عامة في السيناريوهات التي تم تشغيلها.
- لا يمكن اعتماد الشكل الحالي كمرجع بصري نهائي قبل إغلاق هذه المشاكل.

## التوكنز والـSCSS

التحليل الشامل غطّى **191 مصدراً يحتوي على Styles**:

- 41 ملف SCSS.
- 150 inline-style source.
- 123 custom property معلنة.
- 155 custom property مستخدمة.
- 257 استخداماً لألوان literal.
- 102 لون literal مختلف.
- 510 استخدامات لـborder-radius.
- 39 قيمة Radius مختلفة.
- 38 استخداماً لـz-index.
- 17 قيمة z-index مختلفة.
- 173 Media Query.
- 27 استخداماً لـ`!important`.

هذا يؤكد أن هناك Design-System foundation حقيقية، لكنها ليست بعد مرجعاً موحداً كافياً لإعادة التصميم على مستوى النظام.

## المخاطر العالية

لا توجد مشكلة مصنفة Critical دون دليل تنفيذي. توجد **7 مخاطر High**:

1. غموض وضخامة Public API وتعدد مسارات التصدير.
2. وجود معماريتين متوازيتين: العملاء الحديثة والصفحات القديمة العملاقة.
3. تجاوز Primitives داخل UI Business وWeb.
4. تداخل نماذج Actions/Lifecycle/Bulk/Output دون Vocabulary موحدة بالكامل.
5. تفتت Tokens/Themes/Breakpoints/Radii.
6. تعارض وثائق React/Angular ووجود أوامر ومسارات قديمة.
7. عدم خضرة بوابات Showcase البصرية والتفاعلية حتى الآن.

# 3. CORE IMPLEMENTATION PHILOSOPHY

Preserve strong behavior.

Refactor weak architecture.

Replace poor visual expression.

Do not rewrite working infrastructure without evidence.

The target is:

> zero duplicated UX logic

NOT:

> zero-code pages

And the component rule is:

> composition over universal God Components.

Configuration must remain semantic and controlled.

Do NOT expose arbitrary page-level:

- padding,
- margin,
- radius,
- colors,
- font sizes,
- hover colors,
- icon gaps,
- shadows,
- control heights.

Those are Design System responsibilities.

Feature consumers may configure:

- semantic variant,
- size,
- density,
- state,
- capabilities,
- data,
- actions,
- templates,
- explicitly supported extension points.

---

# 4. ABSOLUTE ARCHITECTURAL RULES

These rules are mandatory.

## 4.1 UI independence

The UI package must not import:

- API Client,
- Web,
- HttpClient,
- backend services,
- feature services.

The dependency direction must remain one-way.

## 4.2 Feature knowledge

Generic UI must not know:

- Customer,
- Supplier,
- Warehouse,
- Shipping Company,
- employee feature APIs,
- backend routes.

## 4.3 Business components

ERP business components may know ERP concepts such as:

- journal lines,
- payment allocation,
- stock adjustment,
- commercial lines,
- workflows,

but they must compose established UI primitives rather than reimplement controls.

## 4.4 Application infrastructure

These stay Web-owned:

- API execution,
- authentication execution,
- permission resolution,
- route guards,
- session orchestration,
- branch orchestration,
- HTTP behavior,
- startup orchestration,
- offline execution queue,
- backend concurrency execution.

UI may provide presentation contracts/surfaces only.

---

# 5. TARGET CONCEPTUAL LAYERING

Use the following conceptual ownership model.

Physical folder/package moves are allowed where they improve the architecture, but avoid gratuitous churn.

```text
Foundation
    ↓
Primitives
    ↓
Forms / Data / Feedback / Overlays / Navigation
    ↓
Composite Components
    ↓
Generic UI Patterns
    ↓
Generic ERP Patterns
    ↓
Domain ERP Business UI
    ↓
Web Application Infrastructure
    ↓
Web Features
```

Definitions:

## Foundation

- semantic tokens;
- theme contracts;
- typography;
- spacing;
- radii;
- elevation;
- motion;
- z-index;
- breakpoints;
- density;
- shell dimensions;
- icon contracts.

## Primitives

Examples:

- Button;
- Icon Button;
- Icon;
- basic status/display primitives.

## Forms

Examples:

- Text Input;
- Number Input;
- Password Input;
- Textarea;
- Date/Time;
- Checkbox;
- Radio;
- Switch;
- Select family;
- Form Field;
- validation;
- uploads;
- repeater.

## Data

Examples:

- Money;
- DateTime;
- Pagination;
- Smart Table;
- Card List;
- Columns;
- Column Chooser;
- Data Page.

## Feedback

Examples:

- Alert;
- Empty;
- Error;
- Loading;
- Skeleton;
- Toast;
- confirmation/conflict visuals.

## Overlays

- Drawer;
- Modal;
- Tooltip;
- shared focus/stack behavior.

## Navigation

- navigation contracts;
- Navigation Tree;
- route-independent expansion/render behavior.

## Generic UI Patterns

Examples:

- Standard Entity Form mechanics;
- wizard/review;
- generic data exploration composition.

## Generic ERP Patterns

Examples:

- Entity Directory;
- Entity Detail;
- Entity Output;
- ERP action placement.

These are ERP-level concepts but are not Accounting/Inventory/Sales-specific.

## Domain ERP Business UI

Examples:

- Journal Lines Editor;
- Payment Allocation;
- Stock Adjustment;
- Sale/Purchase Lines;
- Permission Tree;
- domain workflow panels.

## Shell

Shell is a stable cross-cutting application-frame family that may compose Foundation, primitives, navigation and overlays but never Web features.

The conceptual layering above does NOT require gratuitously moving every file.

- tests/imports can be migrated safely.

# 7. CANONICAL PUBLIC API RULES

The current package has too many ambiguous public paths.

Implement canonical ownership.

## 7.1 One canonical import path

Every supported public symbol must have one canonical public import path.

Compatibility re-exports may remain temporarily, but must be:

- explicitly documented,
- clearly marked deprecated,
- never used by new internal application code.

Update UI Showcase and Web to use canonical imports where practical in this phase.

## 7.2 Compatibility

Do not break all consumers at once.

For an existing public symbol being relocated:

1. preserve a compatibility export;
2. add an explicit deprecation note;
3. point documentation to the canonical location;
4. update internal repository consumers;
5. add/update governance checks preventing new legacy imports.

## 7.3 Suggested canonical ownership

Use repository evidence to finalize exact details, but follow this direction:

- `honesty-erp-ui/icons`
  - semantic icon API.

- `honesty-erp-ui/essentials`
  - startup-safe primitives;
  - Button;
  - low-level actions/contracts as required to avoid cycles;
  - overlays if dependency order requires them.

- `honesty-erp-ui/forms`
  - all form controls and Form Engine public surface.

- `honesty-erp-ui/data-display`
  - data contracts, formatting/display, table/data controls.

- `honesty-erp-ui/feedback`
  - canonical consumer-facing feedback API.

- `honesty-erp-ui/business`
  - ERP patterns/business surfaces.

- `honesty-erp-ui`
  - Shell;
  - Navigation;
  - action composition;
  - authorization presentation;
  - cross-entry compatibility surface only where necessary.

Do not allow the root barrel to become an uncontrolled export-all package.

# 11. DESIGN SYSTEM V2 TOKEN MODEL

Create one authoritative token contract.

At minimum include the following categories.

## Colors

Semantic only:

```text
canvas
surface
surface-raised
surface-subtle
surface-hover
surface-selected

text-primary
text-secondary
text-muted
text-disabled
text-inverse

border-subtle
border-default
border-strong

action-primary
action-primary-hover
action-primary-active
action-secondary

focus-ring

success
success-surface
warning
warning-surface
danger
danger-surface
info
info-surface
```

Light and Dark themes define values.

Components consume semantic roles.

## Typography

Centralize:

- font family;
- monospace if genuinely required;
- sizes;
- weights;
- line heights;
- numeric/tabular behavior.

Use Cairo as the primary Arabic UI font unless repository evidence requires an intentional different product font.

Use a compact, clear scale.

Do not allow arbitrary `.8125`, `.84375`, `.875`, etc. to proliferate without semantic justification.

## Spacing

One governed spacing scale.

## Radius

Reduce uncontrolled radii drastically.

Use a compact semantic scale similar in concept to:

- small,
- medium,
- large,
- extra-large,
- full/circular.

Exact values are yours to determine from the rendered redesign.

Pill/full values are allowed only for components where that geometry is semantically appropriate.

## Elevation

Create governed elevation levels.

## Motion

Create named duration/easing tokens.

Respect reduced-motion behavior already present.

## Z-index

Create a named layer model, for example conceptually:

- content;
- sticky;
- header;
- sidebar;
- dropdown;
- drawer/modal;
- tooltip/toast.

Do not use arbitrary `9999`.

## Density/control dimensions

Centralize:

- control heights;
- button heights;
- icon-button sizes;
- toolbar height;
- table row density;
- sidebar item height;
- topbar height;
- common icon sizes.

## Breakpoints

Centralize SCSS breakpoints/mixins.

Do not maintain dozens of unrelated media-query thresholds.

Desktop acceptance priorities:

1. 1920×1080
2. 1440×900
3. 1366×768
4. 1024×768

Mobile Web must remain usable but is NOT the primary V2 visual target.

# 12. TOKEN MIGRATION RULES

Within the UI library:

- eliminate uncontrolled literal colors;
- eliminate arbitrary radii;
- eliminate arbitrary z-index values;
- consolidate breakpoints;
- remove unnecessary `!important`;
- use logical RTL properties;
- use component-local CSS variables only for legitimate component variants derived from foundation semantics.

Do NOT mechanically turn every pixel value into a token.

A component may still need intrinsic values such as:

- 1px border;
- full circle 50%;
- layout math.

But repeated design decisions must become tokens.

# 19. SIDEBAR / DESKTOP BEHAVIOR

The current 1024 layout retains a full expanded sidebar and compresses content.

Fix this.

Target behavior:

## >= 1280px

Normal expanded desktop sidebar is acceptable by default.

## 1024px–1279px

Prefer compact/collapsed desktop sidebar behavior rather than consuming full desktop width.

It must remain quickly expandable.

## Below the established desktop boundary

Use overlay navigation behavior.

Do not spend disproportionate effort on phone-specific Web polish.

Navigation rules:

- approximately three hierarchy levels is the normal UX content rule;
- deeper technical nesting support may remain;
- active state must be strong and unambiguous;
- parent/child hierarchy must be visually obvious;
- collapsed state must remain understandable through icons/tooltips;
- permission pruning stays Web-owned.

# 20. PAGE HEADER STANDARD

Create one consistent Page Header hierarchy.

For RTL:

- identity/title area on the logical start/right;
- action area on the logical end/left.

Support:

- icon;
- title;
- subtitle;
- breadcrumbs;
- primary action;
- secondary actions;
- overflow/output actions;
- optional contextual metadata.

Use a compact breadcrumb treatment integrated into the Page Header visual hierarchy unless technical evidence strongly requires separate placement.

Action hierarchy:

- one dominant Primary action per action group;
- Create/New: Primary;
- Save: Primary;
- Cancel: Secondary;
- Delete/destructive: Danger;
- Print/Export: grouped output/menu behavior;
- Refresh: utility/icon action where appropriate.

Do not let each feature decide its own order.

# 60. HARD-BLOCKER RULE

Do not label ordinary implementation difficulty as a blocker.

These are NOT blockers:

- TypeScript errors caused by your changes;
- failed unit tests;
- failed E2E;
- SCSS regression;
- snapshot mismatch caused by your intentional redesign;
- circular dependency created during refactor;
- broken import;
- build budget warning;
- missing component Showcase case.

Fix them.

A genuine HARD BLOCKER requires something such as:

- unavailable credential;
- unavailable external/private infrastructure;
- destructive production-data decision;
- ambiguous financial/business semantic rule that cannot be inferred safely from existing code/tests/contracts.

If such a blocker exists:

1. isolate it;
2. complete every unaffected part;
3. document exact evidence;
4. leave the repository otherwise green.

Do not optimize for speed.

Optimize for:

- correctness;
- consistency;
- maintainability;
- visual coherence;
- stable APIs;
- reusable behavior;
- testability;
- future migration of hundreds of ERP screens.

Do not stop after the first working version.

Build it.

Render it.

Inspect it.

Test it.

Correct it.

Repeat until the Foundation V2 phase is genuinely complete.
