# Honesty ERP Design System V2

> Implemented specification — 2026-09-20  
> Source of truth: `src/frontend/angular/ui/src/styles/`

## 1. Design character

Foundation V2 is Arabic-first, RTL-first and desktop-first. It is designed for long ERP work sessions: calm surfaces, dense but legible information, restrained elevation, clear hierarchy, stable interaction states and an indigo action identity. It avoids decorative glass, excessive gradients, oversized cards, arbitrary rounding and per-page visual tuning.

Behavioral contracts are preserved where they were strong; visual values are centralized and intentionally replace inconsistent legacy expression.

## 2. Token authority

The authoritative files are:

- `_tokens.scss`: typography, spacing, shape, elevation, motion, density, dimensions, z-index and compatibility aliases;
- `_themes.scss`: semantic Light/Dark color values;
- `_breakpoints.scss`: named SCSS breakpoints and mixins;
- `_foundation.scss`: global typography, focus, control and reduced-motion behavior;
- `_entities.scss`: shared entity-pattern geometry;
- `_index.scss`: public style composition.

Components consume `--honesty-*` semantic roles. A page may choose semantic tone, size, density, state and capability; it may not configure arbitrary padding, radius, color, shadow, font size, hover color or control height.

## 3. Color system

Both themes implement the same semantic roles:

| Family | Roles |
|---|---|
| canvas/surfaces | `canvas`, `surface`, `surface-raised`, `surface-subtle`, `surface-muted`, `surface-hover`, `surface-selected`, `backdrop` |
| text | `text-primary`, `text-secondary`, `text-muted`, `text-disabled`, `text-inverse`, `text-on-action`, `text-on-status` |
| borders | `border-subtle`, `border-default`, `border-strong` |
| action | `action-primary`, `action-primary-hover`, `action-primary-active`, `action-secondary`, `action-secondary-hover`, `action-disabled`, `accent`, `focus-ring` |
| status | success/info/warning/danger/neutral foreground and soft-surface pairs |
| shell | sidebar surface/text/active/border and header surface |

Light theme uses a neutral cool canvas, white working surfaces, dark slate text and controlled indigo actions. Dark theme is deep blue-slate rather than pure black, with elevated surfaces and sufficient text/border contrast. Status colors communicate meaning; warning colors are not used as generic navigation hover.

No component should bind directly to a palette color when a semantic role exists. Intrinsic literals are permitted for transparent mixing or preserved approved template fidelity and must remain documented.

## 4. Typography

- Primary Arabic UI: `Cairo`, then `Public Sans`, then system sans-serif.
- Monospace: `Cascadia Code`, `SFMono-Regular`, Consolas, monospace.
- Scale: 2xs, xs, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl, 3xl.
- Weights: 400, 500, 600, 700.
- Line heights: tight, body, relaxed.
- Monetary/identifier values should use tabular numerals when alignment matters.
- Headings establish hierarchy by weight and restrained size; body rhythm is not manufactured through random local font sizes.

## 5. Spacing and layout rhythm

The spacing scale follows a four-pixel base rhythm, with named half steps only where compact controls require them. It ranges from 0 through 4rem. Components use logical `padding-inline`, `margin-inline`, `inset-inline-*` and `block-*` properties.

Rules:

- adjacent label/help/error text uses the small steps;
- controls and compact toolbars use 2–4 steps;
- cards/sections use 4–6 steps;
- page regions use 6–10 steps depending on viewport;
- do not introduce a new repeated spacing value inside a component without first checking the scale.

## 6. Radius

Governed scale:

| Token | Intended use |
|---|---|
| `radius-xs` | tiny internal markers |
| `radius-sm` | compact controls/chips |
| `radius-md` | standard controls and buttons |
| `radius-lg` | cards, drawers and structured panels |
| `radius-xl` | major contained surfaces only |
| `radius-full` | circular icons, avatars, pills only |

Generic cards are not automatically pills. Components should not expose radius as a consumer input.

## 7. Elevation

Named shadows are `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` and `overlay`. Borders and surface contrast are preferred over heavy shadows. Menus, selects and compact popovers normally use `md`; modal/drawer overlays use `overlay`. Static content cards normally use no more than `xs` or `sm`.

## 8. Motion

Durations are `instant` (80ms), `fast` (140ms), `base` (200ms) and `slow` (320ms), with standard and emphasized easing. Movement communicates state rather than decoration. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` disables nonessential transitions and spinner animation fallbacks remain understandable via status text.

## 9. Z-index

Named layers govern content, sticky regions, header/sidebar, dropdown, overlay and tooltip/toast stacking. Arbitrary `9999` values are prohibited. A new layer requires evidence that the existing model cannot express the relationship.

## 10. Density and control dimensions

Control heights are centralized:

- small: 2.25rem;
- medium/default: 2.75rem;
- large: 3rem;
- extra-large: 3.5rem.

Icon sizes, inline control padding, toolbar height, table row density, Sidebar item height and shell dimensions use tokens. `sm`, `md` and `lg` are semantic density selections, not arbitrary pixel overrides.

## 11. Breakpoints and desktop policy

Named breakpoints:

| Name | Value | Primary meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `compact` | 40rem | compact/mobile-web fallback |
| `medium` | 64rem | 1024px desktop acceptance boundary |
| `wide` | 85.375rem | 1366px working width |
| `xwide` | 90rem | 1440px preferred workspace |
| `full` | 120rem | 1920px large workspace |

Use `honesty-breakpoint-up`, `-down` and `-between`. Do not add one-off media thresholds for cosmetic differences.

Priority matrix is 1920×1080, 1440×900, 1366×768 and 1024×768. At 1024–1279 the Sidebar uses compact desktop behavior; below desktop it becomes an overlay. Mobile Web remains usable but is not the V2 visual optimization target.

## 12. Focus and interaction states

Every interactive primitive provides:

- visible `:focus-visible` ring derived from `focus-ring`;
- hover, active, disabled and busy states;
- accessible name and applicable ARIA disclosure state;
- disabled reason where policy supplies one;
- keyboard behavior appropriate to the semantic control;
- target sizes enforced by Showcase quality tests.

Focus is never removed without an equivalent. Tooltip is available on hover and keyboard focus. Overlays restore focus and respond to Escape.

## 13. Button and Icon Button

Button tones: primary, secondary, success, warning, danger and neutral. Variants: solid, outline and ghost. Sizes: sm, md and lg.

Rules:

- one dominant primary action per local decision region;
- secondary actions use outline or restrained solid treatment;
- tertiary/overflow actions use ghost/menu placement;
- destructive actions use danger and, where required, confirmation policy;
- Icon Button always has an accessible action label and is used only when the icon is unambiguous;
- busy state blocks repeat invocation and exposes `aria-busy`;
- full-width is a layout capability, not a visual-value escape hatch.

## 14. Form controls

Text, number, password, textarea, date/time, checkbox, radio, switch and select family share height, padding, border, focus, invalid, disabled, readonly and typography contracts.

Rules:

- labels and errors are associated programmatically;
- required/invalid state must not rely on color alone;
- server validation is mapped by Web/form workflow into the same field and summary surfaces;
- Checkbox/Radio preserve the approved template appearance and vertical centering;
- native date placeholders are not exposed as the Arabic product experience; controlled segmented Arabic presentation retains stable ISO-like values and min/max validation;
- custom controls implement CVA rather than maintaining a parallel form state.

## 15. Select family

Three intentionally distinct controls exist:

- `ErpSelect`: local single selection;
- `ErpMultiSelect`: local multiple selection with chips;
- `ErpRemoteSelect`: server-backed selection with cancellation, stale-response protection and hydration.

Shared features include searchable options, groups, semantic icons, avatars/images, disabled options, loading, no-results, clearing and RTL-safe open panels. Every trigger and clear action must have an operational name; clear targets satisfy the quality gate.

The shell branch selector uses startup-safe `ErpStartupSelect` to avoid a dependency cycle. It is not a fourth feature-level select API.

## 16. Page Header and action hierarchy

Page Header integrates breadcrumbs in a compact hierarchy. In RTL:

- identity/title is at logical start/right;
- action group is at logical end/left;
- one primary action leads;
- secondary actions follow;
- output/overflow actions are grouped rather than scattered;
- contextual metadata remains optional and concise.

The header does not contain list refresh; refresh belongs to the data toolbar so active filters/query state remain intact.

## 17. Data and tables

- Smart Table owns table rendering, sorting intent, row selection and responsive containment—not data fetching.
- At 1024, horizontal overflow is contained within the table surface and never clips the page or Sidebar.
- Card List is a first-class alternate representation supplied through an explicit renderer.
- Column chooser, pagination, filters and bulk actions are composed capabilities.
- Toolbar controls that depend on records are hidden when no rows are displayed.
- Loading, empty, no-results and error states use canonical feedback visuals.
- KPI cards use controlled tone, icon position/size, trend, chips, substats and progress; arbitrary card styling is not accepted.

## 18. Feedback

Alert, Empty, Error, Loading, Skeleton, Async Content, Toast, Confirmation, Conflict and Offline surfaces share semantic tones, typography and spacing. Context patterns may orchestrate state, but do not redraw their own empty/error/loading visuals.

Empty State distinguishes no-data, no-results and custom situations and can expose a controlled action. Error State exposes actionable retry only when the caller can actually retry.

## 19. Overlays

Modal and Drawer use semantic surface, backdrop, elevation, radius and header/footer rhythm. Drawer sides use logical start/end. Tooltip is concise assistance, never the sole carrier of required information. Select/menu panels share governed overlay stacking.

All overlays preserve keyboard focus, Escape, outside-click policy, restoration and reduced motion.

## 20. RTL rules

- Root direction is RTL for production Arabic UI.
- Use logical properties; physical left/right are allowed only for intrinsically directional art.
- Do not mirror checkmarks, phone numbers, numeric identifiers or icons whose meaning would change.
- Direction-sensitive values declare `dir=ltr` or `auto` at the value boundary.
- Breadcrumb ordering remains logically understandable in RTL.
- badges use logical inset properties.
- Arabic long text and wrapped identifiers are part of Showcase and Customer evidence.

## 21. Theme switching and fonts

Theme values switch under `[data-theme='dark']`; component contracts do not fork by theme. The rendered evidence confirms Light/Dark parity. Essential fonts and icons must load without failed asset requests. Semantic `ng-icons` references prevent vendor names leaking into features.

## 22. Governance and current metrics

The V2 scan covers 117 style sources: 15 SCSS files plus 102 inline component style blocks. It found 219 declared and 195 used custom properties, 121 hard-color occurrences, 26 unique radii across 279 occurrences, 13 unique z-index values across 33 occurrences, 34 unique media queries across 110 occurrences, and 19 `!important` occurrences.

The audit baseline scanner covered only 30 external SCSS files, not inline styles. Therefore raw counts are not a like-for-like regression comparison. Safe observations are that V2 now has one authoritative semantic contract, governed breakpoints/z-index/radius layers, and `!important` did not increase (20 baseline occurrences versus 19 in the broader V2 scan). Preserved Checkbox/Radio template styles account for a meaningful portion of approved literal colors.

Raw evidence: `v2-artifacts/data/v2-token-metrics.json` and `v2-artifacts/reports/v2-token-report.md`.

## 23. Prohibited replacements

Do not create feature-local styled replacements for Button, Icon Button, Select, Checkbox/Radio, inputs, Drawer, Modal, Tooltip, Empty/Error/Loading, table controls, Page Header, Entity Directory, Entity Detail or Standard Entity Form when the canonical behavior fits.

An exception requires a behavioral reason, a documented boundary and tests. Cosmetic preference is not a reason.






# Honesty ERP — Feature Migration Contract

> Applies after Frontend Foundation V2.  
> Reference implementation: `src/frontend/angular/web/src/app/features/sales/customers`.

## 1. Scope

This contract defines how a legacy or new Web feature adopts Foundation V2. It does not authorize mass migration. Features migrate one bounded domain at a time after Customers remains green.

The goal is zero duplicated UX logic, not zero-code pages. Shared visual/interaction behavior belongs in UI; API mapping, business rules, permissions, branch context and execution belong in Web/feature code.

## 2. Expected conventional entity structure

Names may adapt to the domain, but responsibilities must remain separated:

```text
feature/
├── feature.routes.ts
├── list/
│   ├── entity-list.page.ts
│   ├── entity-list.state.ts
│   ├── entity-list.presenter.ts
│   ├── entity-list.policy.ts
│   ├── entity-list.adapter.ts
│   └── entity-list.output.ts
├── form/
│   ├── entity-form.page.ts
│   ├── entity-form.state.ts
│   ├── entity-form.workflow.ts
│   ├── entity-form.schema.ts
│   ├── entity-form.adapter.ts
│   └── custom-renderers/        # only when required
├── detail/
│   ├── entity-detail.page.ts
│   ├── entity-detail.state.ts
│   ├── entity-detail.schema.ts
│   ├── entity-detail.presenter.ts
│   └── custom-renderers/        # only when required
├── data-access/
│   ├── entity.api.ts
│   └── entity.models.ts
└── shared/                      # feature-only helpers, not a shadow UI library
```

A file split is justified by responsibility, not line-count cosmetics. Small coherent collaborators may be combined; Page must not become the state/API/policy/presenter/workflow God Class.

## 3. Ownership matrix

| Concern | UI package | Web cross-cutting | Feature |
|---|---|---|---|
| tokens, themes, primitive visuals | owns | consumes | consumes |
| table/form/entity-pattern rendering | owns | consumes | configures/composes |
| OpenAPI DTO/service | forbidden | provides/generated | imports through adapter/data access |
| HTTP/API execution | forbidden | infrastructure | invokes typed adapter |
| authentication/session | presentation only | owns | observes resolved state |
| permission/branch/capability resolution | contracts only | infrastructure | policy resolves for domain |
| business validation/calculation | no | shared only if truly cross-domain | owns |
| route/query synchronization | no | router infrastructure | owns screen mapping |
| loading/empty/error visuals | owns | orchestrates global states | selects state/message/retry intent |
| server validation mapping | visual contracts | shared mapper if generic | maps API problem to form |
| output/print/export presentation | pattern owns | transport support | scope/query/document rules |
| concurrency execution | dialog/surface | transport policy | entity workflow |

## 4. Dependency rules

Allowed:

```text
feature page → feature state/workflow/presenter/policy/adapter
feature collaborators → API Client and Web infrastructure
feature rendering → canonical UI entry points
UI business pattern → UI forms/data/feedback/essentials/icons
```

Forbidden:

```text
UI → API Client / HttpClient / Web / feature
feature A → feature B internals
primitive → composite/pattern
shell → feature
feature → UI internal src/lib path
feature → ng-icons vendor import
```

Cross-feature data must flow through an approved application service or generated API contract, not a relative import into another feature.

## 5. List/Directory contract

A migrated entity list must:

1. define a typed server query/filter/sort/page state;
2. map API DTOs to a stable row view model in an adapter/presenter;
3. provide row identity and column contracts;
4. supply an `ErpEntityDirectoryConfig`;
5. handle its single discriminated intent stream;
6. preserve filters when refreshing;
7. use true server total count—never current-page length;
8. hide row-dependent toolbar controls when no rows are displayed;
9. distinguish no-data, no-results, loading and error;
10. recheck `contextKey`, branch and authority before executing an intent;
11. provide table/card renderers only where both are meaningful;
12. implement output scopes and bulk results explicitly.

Server-side pagination, sorting and filtering are the default. Client-side filtering is allowed only for a clearly bounded already-loaded option/list and must be documented.

## 6. Detail contract

A migrated detail page must:

- map DTO to a readonly detail view model;
- define hero, facts, KPI, tabs, section, audit and rail schemas;
- keep section API loading in State, not resolver/template code;
- supply redacted values after permission resolution;
- use custom renderers only for genuinely domain-specific content;
- wrap long Arabic text, identifiers, email/phone and monetary values correctly;
- verify 1024 and 1440 layouts;
- keep actions in the shared action vocabulary.

Rails are optional. Do not reserve empty columns for aesthetic symmetry.

## 7. Create/Edit form contract

For a conventional entity:

1. Page binds route/entity identity and composes the shell/header/form.
2. State owns the current entity, reference data and asynchronous status.
3. Workflow owns step transitions, validation, submit, cancel, conflict and result.
4. Schema describes conventional fields/sections/steps.
5. Adapter maps DTO ↔ form model/request; generated DTOs do not become the form model by accident.
6. Policy resolves field/action visibility and editability.
7. Custom renderers implement only the exceptional domain input.

Use `ErpStandardEntityForm` where the form is conventional. Complex ERP transactions may compose primitives and domain editors directly. Never evolve the schema into a second programming language to avoid writing a clear custom component.

## 8. API mapping

- Generated API Client is immutable/generated infrastructure.
- Feature API adapter is the only place that knows operation signatures and DTO quirks.
- UI view models use stable domain/presentation names and null semantics.
- Dates/timezones, money/precision and enum mappings are explicit.
- Cancellation/stale response protection is required for remote search.
- A branch/tenant context failure is handled by Web infrastructure and retriable state, not hidden in a UI control.

Do not pass API services, URLs, Observables tied to HttpClient or generated request DTOs into UI components.

## 9. Permissions and field authorization

Permission flow:

```text
session + claims + branch + capability + entity lifecycle
  → feature Policy/Security resolver
  → field/action availability + redacted view model
  → UI rendering
  → intent
  → authority/context recheck
  → execution
```

Rules:

- hiding a button is not authorization;
- field-level sensitive values are redacted before entering generic UI;
- disabled reasons are user-facing and do not expose security internals;
- lifecycle transitions use explicit resolved actions;
- branch changes invalidate stale pages/intents;
- unauthorized output scopes are not offered or sent.

## 10. Validation

Client validation uses Angular Reactive Forms and primitive CVAs. Cross-field/domain rules live in the form workflow/domain validator. Server validation is mapped into:

- matching field errors when a reliable field path exists;
- validation summary for cross-field/general errors;
- explicit retry/error state for transport/server failures.

Do not swallow the server problem, clear valid user input, or create a second independent validation state in the page template.

## 11. Concurrency

Edit/transition requests carry the backend concurrency token expected by the API. On conflict:

- workflow pauses normal success handling;
- canonical conflict surface shows the meaningful choices;
- feature decides reload/compare/overwrite legality;
- authority and token are revalidated before a retry;
- UI dialog does not execute HTTP itself.

## 12. Unsaved changes

Form workflow registers dirty state with Web unsaved-change orchestration. Cancel/navigation:

- exits directly when pristine;
- requests a canonical confirmation when dirty;
- preserves the form if the user stays;
- unregisters after successful save/destruction.

Header save/cancel invokes the same Wizard validation and unsaved-change paths as in-form controls; it is not a bypass.

## 13. Actions and output

Define actions once as `ErpActionPolicy`, resolve `ErpActionAvailability` in Policy/State, render in the appropriate placement, then handle `ErpActionInvocation` in Workflow/Page.

Print/export:

- is grouped under one Output surface;
- exposes only permitted formats/scopes;
- selected/page/all-results scope is explicit;
- the feature/API adapter owns server generation/download;
- results/failures are explicit;
- no client export silently substitutes current page for all results.

## 14. Styling and native controls

- Use semantic V2 tokens and shared entity classes.
- Feature styles may define domain layout, not a parallel design system.
- No arbitrary shared-component padding/radius/color overrides.
- Use logical RTL properties.
- Use ERP Button/Icon Button, form controls, selects, overlays and feedback.
- Native semantic elements inside a primitive are correct; feature-level styled replacements are not.

Any intentional exception must identify missing behavior, why composition is insufficient, and the planned reusable boundary.

## 15. Showcase and tests

A migration must add/update:

- unit tests for adapter, policy, presenter/state/workflow and schema rules;
- page/component integration tests;
- E2E for route, success, empty, error, permission and key workflow paths;
- Light/Dark RTL screenshots at 1440 and 1024 for changed archetypes;
- Showcase only when a public shared component/pattern changes;
- governance expectations if a new legitimate boundary is introduced.

Do not weaken Axe, visual, permission or boundary checks to pass the migration.

## 16. Acceptance checklist per feature

- [ ] Lazy route is the feature’s only external reachability point.
- [ ] No cross-feature internal imports.
- [ ] Page is composition, not API/state/policy God Class.
- [ ] Generated DTOs are mapped at the feature boundary.
- [ ] UI receives no backend service or URL.
- [ ] Server pagination/filter/sort and true totals are correct.
- [ ] Branch/context invalidation is handled.
- [ ] Action and field permissions are resolved and rechecked.
- [ ] List uses Entity Directory where appropriate.
- [ ] Detail uses Entity Detail where appropriate.
- [ ] Conventional form uses Standard Entity Form where appropriate.
- [ ] Complex transaction can opt out cleanly.
- [ ] Canonical feedback/overlays/actions/forms/data controls are used.
- [ ] No unjustified feature-level native-control or icon bypass.
- [ ] Empty/loading/error/no-results states are distinct.
- [ ] Server validation and concurrency are explicit.
- [ ] Unsaved changes protect cancel/navigation.
- [ ] Light/Dark, RTL, 1024 and 1440 are verified.
- [ ] Unit, lint/governance, build and E2E gates pass.
- [ ] Customer Golden Reference remains green after shared changes.

## 17. Recommended migration order

After Foundation V2 is frozen:

1. select one conventional, low-risk entity to validate the contract;
2. migrate a second conventional entity with richer permissions/output;
3. migrate one detail-heavy entity;
4. migrate one complex transaction using domain editors, without forcing Standard Entity Form;
5. only then batch similar legacy entities.

Do not start multiple feature migrations while shared V2 contracts are still changing. A shared defect discovered during migration is fixed in UI, demonstrated in Showcase, and revalidated against Customers before feature work continues.




# Honesty ERP Frontend Foundation V2 — Implemented Architecture

> Status: implemented and verified on 2026-09-20  
> Workspace: `src/frontend/angular`  
> Angular: 21.2.4  
> Golden Reference: `web/src/app/features/sales/customers`

## 1. Purpose and authority

This document describes the architecture that exists after Foundation V2. It is not a proposal. The UI package remains backend-agnostic, Customers remains the only intentionally refined Web feature, and legacy Web features are not implicitly compliant merely because shared styles changed.

The governing direction is:

```text
Foundation
  ├─> Primitives
  │     ├─> Forms / Data / Feedback / Overlays / Navigation
  │     │     ├─> Composite UI
  │     │     │     ├─> Generic UI Patterns
  │     │     │     │     ├─> Generic ERP Patterns
  │     │     │     │     │     └─> Domain ERP Business UI
  │     └─> Shell
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────> Web Application

API Client ───────────────────────────────────────> Web Application
UI ──────────────────────────────────────────────> Web Application
UI -X-> API Client / HttpClient / feature services / Web
```

Evidence:

- dependency/governance check: `src/frontend/angular/tools/ui/check-ui-boundaries.mjs`;
- entity boundaries: `src/frontend/angular/tools/architecture/check-entity-architecture-boundaries.mjs`;
- canonical styles: `src/frontend/angular/ui/src/styles/_tokens.scss`, `_themes.scss`, `_breakpoints.scss`, `_foundation.scss`, `_entities.scss`;
- public inventory: `v2-artifacts/data/v2-public-api.json` and `v2-public-api.csv`.

## 2. Workspace projects and ownership

| Project | Type | Responsibility | May depend on |
|---|---|---|---|
| `honesty-api-client` | Angular library | OpenAPI-generated operations, services and DTOs | Angular/runtime generation dependencies only |
| `honesty-erp-ui` | Angular package with seven entry points | Design system, UI behavior, generic ERP patterns, domain ERP presentation | Angular, `ng-icons`, internal lower UI layers |
| `honesty-erp-ui-showcase` | Angular application | Executable component and pattern contract | UI package only; no backend execution |
| `honesty-erp-web` | Angular application | Startup, auth, routing, permissions, API execution and features | API Client and UI |

The generated API Client and UI are sibling dependencies of Web. UI never imports API Client. Showcase does not serve as production infrastructure.

## 3. UI layers

### 3.1 Foundation

Foundation owns semantic design decisions and compatibility aliases:

- structural tokens: `ui/src/styles/_tokens.scss`;
- theme values: `ui/src/styles/_themes.scss`;
- governed media queries: `ui/src/styles/_breakpoints.scss`;
- global control/focus/reset behavior: `ui/src/styles/_foundation.scss`;
- shared entity pattern layout: `ui/src/styles/_entities.scss`;
- icon contracts and `ng-icons` registry: `ui/icons`.

Foundation contains no feature names, backend types, or page-specific arbitrary style inputs.

### 3.2 Primitives and essentials

`honesty-erp-ui/essentials` is the startup-safe layer. It contains:

- `ErpButton` and action contracts;
- startup/system feedback surfaces;
- startup-safe overlays;
- `ErpStartupSelect`, used by the shell branch selector to avoid a package cycle;
- unsaved-change presentation contracts.

`ErpIconButton` and higher action composition remain root-owned because they participate in the broader action/shell package. Both render the same `ErpActionPolicy` and `ErpActionAvailability` vocabulary.

### 3.3 Forms

`honesty-erp-ui/forms` owns CVA-based controls, form structure and form-pattern contracts:

- text, number, password, textarea, date, time and date-time controls;
- checkbox, radio group and switch;
- local single select, local multi-select and remote select;
- form field/section/actions/stepper;
- schema/registry/review/wizard/server-validation/upload/repeater infrastructure;
- `ErpStandardEntityForm`.

Form infrastructure emits UI intent and validation state. It does not call APIs or decide permissions.

### 3.4 Data display

`honesty-erp-ui/data-display` owns:

- data-page, data-source, column, sort, selection and pagination contracts;
- Smart Table, card list, column chooser, filter bar/drawer, table toolbar and view switcher;
- money/date-time/contact/status/KPI/chart presentation.

It receives rows, state and typed events. It does not know endpoint URLs, Customers, Suppliers, or server services.

### 3.5 Feedback and overlays

`honesty-erp-ui/feedback` is the canonical consumer-facing feedback API: alert, async content, confirmation, concurrency, offline, toast and sync surfaces. Startup-safe empty/error/loading surfaces remain in essentials where needed to avoid loading the higher entry point during bootstrap.

Modal, Drawer, Tooltip and overlay support preserve focus handling, Escape/outside-click behavior, focus restoration and reduced motion. Their legacy root paths are compatibility facades only.

### 3.6 Generic ERP patterns

`honesty-erp-ui/business` contains generic ERP patterns and domain ERP presentation:

- Entity Directory, Entity Detail and Entity Output;
- audit timeline, attachment list, print/export presentation;
- commercial/journal/payment/stock editors;
- report filter and workflow panels;
- permission tree.

The generic patterns know ERP concepts such as entity actions, server pages and branch-aware presentation contracts. They still do not execute backend requests or resolve the user’s true authority.

### 3.7 Shell

The root entry point owns App Shell, auth/system shells, Sidebar, Navigation Tree, Topbar, Page Shell/Header/Footer, breadcrumbs, tabs, user/notification/search/theme surfaces and action composition.

Shell may compose Foundation, essentials, icons, navigation and overlays. Shell never imports a Web feature. Web supplies pruned navigation, resolved branch choices and action availability.

## 4. Canonical public entry points

| Entry point | Canonical responsibility | V2 export rows |
|---|---|---:|
| `honesty-erp-ui` | Shell, navigation, cross-entry action composition and compatibility surface | 107 |
| `honesty-erp-ui/essentials` | Startup-safe actions, feedback, overlays and system surfaces | 55 |
| `honesty-erp-ui/icons` | Semantic icon types, registry and renderer | 10 |
| `honesty-erp-ui/feedback` | General feedback and asynchronous-state presentation | 28 |
| `honesty-erp-ui/forms` | Form controls and form patterns | 127 |
| `honesty-erp-ui/data-display` | Data contracts and data presentation | 49 |
| `honesty-erp-ui/business` | Generic ERP and domain ERP presentation patterns | 142 |

The generated V2 inventory records 518 export rows, 515 canonical symbols, 116 Angular components, 5 directives, 2 compatibility aliases and 37 deprecated exports.

Rules:

1. New code imports each symbol from its canonical entry point.
2. Internal UI code may not use legacy root facades for a secondary-entry symbol.
3. Compatibility re-exports carry `@deprecated` guidance and exist only to avoid a flag-day consumer break.
4. Root is not an unrestricted export-all barrel.
5. A symbol becomes public only when its contract is supportable as a versioned package API.

## 5. Compatibility strategy

Foundation V2 narrows rather than abruptly removes previous paths. Deprecated root facades currently cover startup/system surfaces, legacy `HonestyIcon`, feedback loading, overlays, unsaved changes, action policy/Button and system shell aliases. Representative files:

- `ui/src/lib/foundation/honesty-icon.ts`;
- `ui/src/lib/actions/erp-action-policy.ts`;
- `ui/src/lib/actions/erp-button.ts`;
- `ui/src/lib/overlays/erp-drawer.ts`;
- `ui/src/lib/overlays/erp-modal.ts`;
- `ui/src/lib/system/erp-startup-gate.ts`;
- `ui/src/lib/shells/honesty-system-page-shell.ts`.

Removal requires all of the following:

- repository consumers use the canonical entry point;
- migration guidance identifies the replacement;
- a deprecation window has elapsed;
- the public inventory and governance check are updated together;
- a deliberate major-version decision authorizes removal.

`HonestyIcon` is a deprecated type/component alias for canonical `ErpIcon`; the compatibility selector remains while application code uses the `honesty-erp-ui/icons` contract. Vendor icon imports remain private to the icon implementation.

## 6. Action architecture

The stabilized vocabulary is:

```text
ErpActionPolicy (definition; presentation requirements only)
        ↓ Web feature policy/security resolution
ErpActionAvailability (visible, disabled, busy, reason)
        ↓
ErpResolvedAction
        ↓ placement renderer
Button | Icon Button | Menu | Entity/Bulk/Lifecycle/Output placement
        ↓
ErpActionInvocation (action + source)
        ↓ Web feature orchestration
confirmation → API execution → explicit result
```

`ErpActionPolicy` may describe label, semantic icon, tone, variant, placement hints, required permission identifiers, branch/capability/online requirements, confirmation and busy key. Those fields are inputs to a Web resolver; UI does not authenticate or authorize.

Distinct placement components remain distinct. V2 did not create a God Action component. Print/export, entity, lifecycle and bulk actions adapt into the same resolved vocabulary.

## 7. Authorization and permission flow

```text
API/session/branch state (Web)
  → feature Policy/Security resolver (Web)
  → resolved visibility/availability + redacted view model (Web)
  → typed UI contract (UI)
  → intent event (UI)
  → recheck context/authority and execute (Web)
```

UI presentation hints are never an authority boundary. The caller owns field redaction, permitted actions, branch scope and financial-data decisions. Entity Directory’s `contextKey` is an opaque stale-event epoch, not a credential. Intent handlers recheck context before executing.

## 8. Forms flow

```text
OpenAPI DTOs (API Client)
  → feature adapter/view model (Web)
  → feature form state/workflow (Web)
  → FormGroup + schema + custom renderer registry
  → ErpStandardEntityForm / primitive CVAs (UI)
  → typed UI intents and client validation
  → feature mapper (Web)
  → API request (Web)
  → server-validation mapping / conflict workflow (Web + UI surface)
```

Conventional fields use schema definitions. Custom sections and field renderers are explicit escape hatches. Complex transactions may compose primitives/editors directly and are not forced through `ErpStandardEntityForm`. Business calculations remain in feature/domain logic.

## 9. Data flow

```text
Route/query/filter/sort/branch state (Web)
  → API adapter and server request (Web)
  → ErpDataPageResult + load state + total count (UI contract)
  → Entity Directory
       ├─ KPI summary
       ├─ Filter Drawer
       ├─ Smart Table / Card List
       ├─ selection + bulk action bar
       ├─ output scope
       └─ pagination
  → typed intent event
  → state transition and new server request (Web)
```

Server pagination, filtering and sorting stay Web-owned. UI never invents a total from the current page. Empty, no-result, loading and error states are explicit. Tools whose meaning depends on records are hidden when there is no displayed data.

## 10. Shell and navigation flow

Web owns route definitions, route activation, permission pruning, branch orchestration and persistence policy. UI owns rendering, hierarchy, compact/expanded/overlay behavior and emits navigation intent.

Viewport behavior is:

- `>= 1280px`: expanded desktop Sidebar is allowed;
- `1024px–1279px`: compact desktop rail protects content width and remains expandable;
- below the desktop boundary: overlay navigation;
- Page Header integrates breadcrumbs, identity, contextual metadata and ordered actions;
- logical CSS properties maintain RTL-first layout without mirroring icon meaning.

`ErpBranchSelector` composes `ErpStartupSelect`, a minimal startup-safe primitive, because the full Forms entry point would create an unsafe shell/bootstrap dependency. It does not duplicate arbitrary feature selection logic.

## 11. Bootstrap and lazy boundaries

Web boots `WebBootstrap` in `web/src/main.ts`. It starts the startup/session/multi-tab coordinators immediately and defers rendering `App` on immediate, retaining startup gating while reducing the initial bundle. `App` keeps router ownership and defers session-expiry and unsaved-change surfaces until their signals require them:

- `web/src/app/auth/session-expiry-surface.ts`;
- `web/src/app/forms/unsaved-changes-surface.ts`;
- `web/src/app/app.html`.

Showcase boots a minimal router shell in `ui-showcase/src/main.ts` and lazy-loads `ShowcaseApp`. This makes the catalog an executable, production-like contract without forcing all playgrounds into the initial bundle.

## 12. Golden Reference adoption rule

Customers preserves independent Page, State, Workflow, Presenter, Schema, Adapter, Policy and Output collaborators. A future feature must follow `ERP_FEATURE_MIGRATION_CONTRACT.md`; it must not copy customer markup or collapse the reference back into a page God Class.

Shared UI behavior belongs in UI only when it is feature-neutral. API mapping, permission resolution, branch context, business rules and execution stay in Web. Custom renderers are used only for genuine domain differences.

## 13. Enforcement and proof

Automated enforcement includes:

- canonical import and backend-independence checks;
- entity package and runtime-cycle boundaries;
- icon-vendor isolation;
- zero live native interactive controls in UI Business;
- Customer feature isolation and lazy reachability;
- entity style ownership and page-resource checks;
- session proxy governance;
- generated API drift and response-contract checks.

Results are stored in `v2-artifacts/reports/`; inventories and raw metrics are in `v2-artifacts/data/`. The completion report is the authoritative release evidence.





# ERP Frontend Foundation V2 — Completion Report

> Completed: 2026-09-20  
> Branch: `feat/angular-web-rebuild-clean-restart`

## 1. Executive Summary

Frontend Foundation V2 is implemented. The Angular workspace now has canonical package ownership, an RTL-first semantic Design System V2, redesigned primitives/forms/feedback/overlays/shell/data patterns, zero live native interactive controls in UI Business, an expanded executable Showcase, and Customers as the verified list/detail/create/edit Golden Reference.

The phase preserved API and business boundaries, did not mass-migrate legacy features, and closed every mandatory gate: 1,157 unit/component tests, 166 Web E2E tests, 23 Showcase E2E tests, 14 Showcase quality tests, builds, lints, API drift checks, browser runtime inspection and visual evidence.

## 2. Initial Baseline

The verified master audit established four Angular projects on Angular 21.2.4, seven UI entry points, 532 public export rows, 525 canonical symbols, 115 components, 5 directives, 80 page-bearing routes, 63 unique page components and 10 page archetypes.

Baseline gates were API/UI/Showcase/Web builds passing, 1,157 unit tests passing, Web E2E 166/166, Showcase E2E 22/23 due to a preserved visual mismatch, and Showcase quality 13/14 due to Select accessible-name/target-size defects.

Four audit fixes were protected throughout: both `tsconfig.dev.json` files plus the approved Checkbox and Radio SCSS.

## 3. Repository State

Work was performed on `feat/angular-web-rebuild-clean-restart` from `e95d5b82447f150d2f3a4edc8560b98c51126af4`. Existing user work and audit evidence were preserved; no destructive reset/clean was used and no commit was created.

Original evidence remains in `audit-artifacts/`. V2 evidence is in `v2-artifacts/`. Intentional source/snapshot/doc changes remain visible in the working tree for review.

## 4. Architecture Changes

The implemented dependency direction is Foundation → Primitives → Forms/Data/Feedback/Overlays/Navigation → Composites → Generic UI Patterns → Generic ERP Patterns → Domain ERP Business UI, with Shell as a stable cross-cutting family. Web consumes UI and API Client; UI consumes neither Web nor API Client/HttpClient/feature services.

Governance now checks 1,599 source files, entity package/runtime boundaries, canonical imports and UI Business native controls. Detailed architecture is in `ERP_FRONTEND_V2_ARCHITECTURE.md`.

## 5. Canonical Public API

The seven canonical entry points and V2 export-row counts are:

| Entry point | Rows |
|---|---:|
| `honesty-erp-ui` | 107 |
| `honesty-erp-ui/essentials` | 55 |
| `honesty-erp-ui/icons` | 10 |
| `honesty-erp-ui/feedback` | 28 |
| `honesty-erp-ui/forms` | 127 |
| `honesty-erp-ui/data-display` | 49 |
| `honesty-erp-ui/business` | 142 |

V2 inventory: 518 export rows, 515 canonical symbols, 116 components, 5 directives, 2 compatibility aliases and 37 deprecated exports. Evidence: `v2-artifacts/data/v2-public-api-summary.json`, `.json` and `.csv`.

## 6. Compatibility Strategy

Relocated public APIs retain narrow `@deprecated` facades with replacement guidance. New internal code uses canonical entry points, and governance rejects accidental legacy secondary-entry imports. Compatibility removal is deferred to a deliberate major-version window after consumer migration.

`HonestyIcon` remains a deprecated alias/selector compatibility path for canonical `ErpIcon`; vendor icon packages remain implementation-private.

## 7. Internalized APIs

Implementation helpers are no longer promoted as preferred public entry points. Root files for startup/system surfaces, loading, overlays, action policy/Button, unsaved changes and system shell are compatibility facades. Internal custom outlets/base implementations remain behind supported semantic wrappers.

No zero-consumer export was deleted merely from static evidence. The generated target/inventory artifacts remain the authority for future removal decisions.

## 8. Action Vocabulary Changes

Action responsibilities now follow: Definition → Resolved Availability → Renderer → Invocation → Confirmation → Execution → Result. `ErpActionPolicy`, `ErpActionAvailability`, `ErpResolvedAction` and `ErpActionInvocation` are shared by Button, Icon Button, menus, entity/lifecycle/bulk and print/export placement.

Web resolves permission, branch, capability, connectivity, lifecycle and busy state, then rechecks before execution. UI presents the result and emits intent; it does not authorize or call the backend.

## 9. Design System V2

V2 provides one semantic contract for Light/Dark colors, Cairo-first typography, spacing, radius, elevation, motion, z-index, density, shell dimensions, icons and breakpoints. Components accept semantic state/variant/size/capability rather than arbitrary visual values.

The implemented specification is `ERP_DESIGN_SYSTEM_V2.md`; sources are `ui/src/styles/_tokens.scss`, `_themes.scss`, `_breakpoints.scss`, `_foundation.scss` and `_entities.scss`.

## 10. Token Changes

The V2 scanner covers 117 style sources (15 SCSS plus 102 inline blocks): 219 declared and 195 used custom properties; 121 hard-color occurrences; 26 unique radii/279 occurrences; 13 unique z-index values/33 occurrences; 34 unique media queries/110 occurrences; and 19 `!important` occurrences.

The audit baseline scanner covered only 30 external SCSS files, so raw counts are not like-for-like. The safe result is semantic centralization and governed scales; `!important` did not increase even with broader V2 coverage (20 baseline versus 19 V2). Approved Checkbox/Radio template fidelity explains many retained literals. Evidence: `v2-artifacts/data/v2-token-metrics.json`.

## 11. Primitive Redesign

ErpIcon, ErpButton, ErpIconButton and status/display primitives now share semantic sizing, focus, disabled/busy states, Light/Dark values and RTL-safe spacing. `ng-icons` vendor references are isolated behind the semantic icon registry; the icon check reports 46 semantic icons.

Button transitions were constrained to avoid transient low-contrast Axe states. Icon Button always obtains an accessible name from its action policy.

## 12. Form Controls

Text, number, password, textarea, checkbox, radio, switch and temporal controls share CVA behavior, control dimensions, focus/invalid/disabled/readonly states and form rhythm. Form sections/actions/stepper and Standard Entity Form use the same token contract.

User-approved Checkbox/Radio appearance and vertical centering were preserved rather than overwritten by a generic restyle.

## 13. Select Family

The three intentional contracts remain: local single `ErpSelect`, local multiple `ErpMultiSelect`, and server-backed `ErpRemoteSelect`. Search, groups, icons, avatars, chips, disabled options, loading, no-results, cancellation, stale-response protection and hydration remain covered.

Operational names and clear target size defects were fixed; Showcase quality is 14/14. Branch Selector uses startup-safe `ErpStartupSelect` to avoid a shell/forms dependency cycle.

## 14. Date/Time UX

Arabic-facing controlled temporal inputs replace reliance on browser-controlled English `mm/dd/yyyy` presentation. Date, time and date-time controls preserve CVA values, min/max, validation, keyboard input and server mapping boundaries. Light/Dark and RTL are verified in Showcase/form scenarios.

## 15. Feedback

Alert, Empty, Error, Loading, Skeleton, Async Content, Toast, Confirmation, Concurrency Conflict, Offline and Sync surfaces use canonical semantic states. Entity/Data patterns orchestrate state but no longer redraw inconsistent feedback primitives.

Empty conditions distinguish no-data/no-results; retry is emitted only through a real caller handler.

## 16. Overlays

Modal, Drawer and Tooltip use governed backdrop, radius, elevation, padding, close affordance and layer tokens. Focus management, Escape, outside-click, restoration and reduced-motion behavior remain. Tooltip now works with keyboard focus as well as pointer hover.

Fresh open-state screenshots exist for Modal, Drawer, Tooltip and Select in both themes.

## 17. Shell V2

App Shell, Sidebar, Topbar, search, branch selector, notifications, user menu, theme toggle, Page Shell/Header/Footer, breadcrumbs, tabs and section surfaces now consume V2 semantics. Shell remains route/feature independent and receives pruned navigation/configuration from Web.

Web’s small bootstrap host starts startup/session/multi-tab orchestration and defers `App`; session-expiry and unsaved-change surfaces are signal-deferred.

## 18. Navigation V2

At >=1280px expanded desktop navigation is allowed. At 1024–1279px compact desktop navigation protects content width and remains expandable. Below the desktop boundary navigation becomes an overlay. Active and parent/child hierarchy remain explicit, with semantic icons and collapsed-state tooltips.

Route activation and permission pruning stay Web-owned.

## 19. Page Shell/Header

Breadcrumbs are integrated into a compact Page Header hierarchy. In RTL, identity is at logical start/right and actions at logical end/left. The header supports icon, title, subtitle, metadata, primary/secondary and output/overflow actions. Data refresh stays in the data toolbar and retains filters.

## 20. Data Foundation

Typed data-page/source/column/sort/selection/pagination contracts remain backend-agnostic. KPI, Money, DateTime, Status, Card List, filter, column and view controls now use V2 tokens and consistent states.

Server-side query ownership remains in Web; UI never guesses all-results total from the current page.

## 21. Smart Table

Smart Table retains rendering, column, sort-intent, selection and state responsibilities without HTTP or feature knowledge. At 1024, horizontal overflow is contained within its surface and no longer compresses/clips the whole page. Pagination, columns, view and bulk capabilities remain composed rather than merged into a God component.

## 22. Entity Directory

Entity Directory composes summary KPIs, filters, table/card view, toolbar, selection/bulk actions, output, pagination and canonical state surfaces. Optional parts are opt-in and never grant permission. A single discriminated event stream carries intent and opaque `contextKey` prevents stale-context handling.

Controls depending on displayed records are absent during empty/no-results states.

## 23. Entity Detail

Entity Detail preserves hero, facts, KPI, tabs, table/timeline/custom sections and renderer registry. Layout refinements remove meaningless fixed rails, improve 1024/1440 geometry and wrap Arabic text/identifiers safely. Direction-sensitive values can declare RTL/LTR/auto.

## 24. Standard Entity Form

Standard Entity Form retains schema/registry/wizard/review/server-validation capabilities with refined section, action and stepper rhythm. It remains appropriate for conventional CRUD and preserves custom fields/sections as escape hatches. Complex transaction editors are not forced through the schema engine.

Header save invokes the same step validation/workflow; cancel uses the unsaved-change guard.

## 25. UI Business Primitive Migration

Commercial Lines, Journal Lines, Payment Allocation, Stock Adjustment, Report Filter, Workflow, Permission Tree, Attachment and related business components now compose ERP controls instead of feature-local native controls. Business calculations were preserved.

Final analyzer: 22 UI Business files, zero occurrences, zero live violations, PASS. Audit baseline was 124 occurrences (88 button, 7 select, 27 input, 2 checkbox). Evidence: `v2-artifacts/data/v2-native-control-report.json`.

## 26. Showcase V2

Showcase is lazy-loaded behind a minimal bootstrap and demonstrates foundation, actions, forms, Select, states, overlays, data, business, security and shell. It includes Light/Dark, RTL, long/dense content, disabled/loading/error/selected/empty states and open interactive overlays.

Final gates: 23/23 functional/visual E2E and 14/14 responsive/accessibility quality across configured Chromium, Edge, Firefox and WebKit coverage.

## 40. Risks

1. Deprecated paths can accumulate if governance exceptions are loosened; keep the inventory and lint rule mandatory.
2. Legacy features can copy Golden Reference markup instead of adopting responsibilities; enforce the migration contract and boundary checks.
3. Schema-driven forms can overgrow into a programming language; retain custom-component escape hatches and direct complex transaction composition.
4. UI presentation hints can be mistaken for authorization; Web must always resolve/recheck authority.
5. Inline styles make metric scope broader and harder to compare; keep the scanner scope explicit.
6. Snapshot replacement can conceal regressions if done casually; preserve before evidence and require intentional review.

No hard blocker remains.

## 41. Future Migration Order

Freeze Customers and Showcase first. Then migrate: one low-risk conventional entity; one entity with richer permissions/output; one detail-heavy entity; one complex transaction using domain editors; finally batches of structurally similar legacy entities. Shared defects return to UI + Showcase + Customer verification before feature work proceeds.

## Architectural decisions implemented

### Canonical entry points

The package keeps seven supported entry points: root, essentials, icons, feedback, forms, data-display and business. Internal repository imports were moved to canonical ownership. Governance rejects new legacy secondary-entry imports.

Root facades required for compatibility were narrowed and marked `@deprecated`. `HonestyIcon` remains a compatibility alias to canonical `ErpIcon`; vendor `ng-icons` imports remain internal.

### Action vocabulary

Action definition, resolved availability, rendered placement, invocation, confirmation, execution and result are now separate responsibilities. `ErpActionPolicy`, `ErpActionAvailability`, `ErpResolvedAction` and `ErpActionInvocation` are shared by Button/Icon Button/menu/entity/lifecycle/bulk/output placements. Web still resolves and executes permissions; UI never authorizes.

### Startup and lazy boundaries

Web uses a small bootstrap host that starts startup/session/multi-tab orchestration immediately and defers `App` rendering. `App` defers session-expiry and unsaved-change surfaces until needed. Showcase uses a minimal router bootstrap and lazy `ShowcaseApp`. This reduced initial bundles while preserving startup gates.

An attempted parent-route lazy App arrangement was rejected because it put the startup gate behind child route evaluation. The implemented `@defer` host keeps startup state visible and router ownership stable.

## Design and component decisions

### Foundation

- one semantic Light/Dark color contract;
- Cairo-first typography and four-pixel spacing rhythm;
- governed radius, elevation, motion, density and z-index scales;
- named breakpoints for compact, 1024, 1366, 1440 and 1920 behavior;
- logical RTL properties and reduced-motion handling;
- shared entity-pattern geometry.

### Primitives and forms

- Button and Icon Button share policy/availability, semantic tones/variants/sizes and accessible busy/disabled behavior;
- form primitives share CVA semantics, heights, focus, invalid/disabled/readonly states;
- Select retains local search/groups/icons/avatars; Multi Select retains chips; Remote Select retains cancellation, stale-response protection and hydration;
- Select accessible names and clear target sizes were fixed;
- Arabic date/time presentation no longer exposes uncontrolled English browser placeholders while preserving stable values and validation;
- approved Checkbox/Radio template styles and vertical centering remain.

### Feedback and overlays

Consumer-facing feedback ownership is canonicalized. Empty/no-result/error/loading states share a visual system. Modal/Drawer/Tooltip use governed backdrop/elevation/radius/z-index and preserve focus, Escape, outside-click and restoration behavior.

### Shell/data/patterns

- 1024–1279 uses compact Sidebar behavior rather than compressing content behind a full rail;
- breadcrumbs are integrated with the Page Header hierarchy;
- Branch Selector composes startup-safe `ErpStartupSelect` to avoid a shell/forms cycle;
- Smart Table contains overflow at 1024 and remains presentation-only;
- row-dependent controls are suppressed when no rows are displayed;
- Card List, KPI, pagination and view switching use the same semantic system;
- Entity Directory, Entity Detail rails/wrapping, and Standard Entity Form were refined without moving API/business execution into UI.

### UI Business

Interactive controls in Commercial Lines, Journal Lines, Payment Allocation, Stock Adjustment, Report Filter, Workflow, Permission Tree, Attachment and related UI Business components now compose V2 primitives. Calculations and business behavior were preserved. The analyzer reports zero live native-control violations across 22 files.

## Bugs discovered and corrected

| Defect | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| Report Filter Panel unstable rendering / NG0103 | template helpers returned new option/value arrays each evaluation | stable model options and cached multi-values |
| blank app after bootstrap refactor (NG05104) | index host selector no longer matched bootstrap component | Web and Showcase index hosts aligned with `erp-bootstrap` and `erp-showcase-bootstrap` |
| startup gates bypassed in lazy experiment | App placed behind parent route/guards | restored direct router config and deferred App inside bootstrap host |
| Web E2E Showcase routes failed | Web Playwright config started only port 4300 while tests also navigate to 4400 | configured dual Web/Showcase servers |
| lazy Showcase focus/count race | tests interacted before lazy root was attached | wait for concrete skip-link/icon attachment, without weakening assertions |
| startup smoke expected eager unsaved surface | surface is intentionally signal-deferred | assertion updated to the new intentional lifecycle |
| Axe transient Button contrast/state issue | background/color transition exposed an intermediate low-contrast state | transition narrowed to non-color geometry/border/shadow behavior |
| temporal accessible labels | segmented controls lacked consistent field association in scenarios | labels/ARIA wiring corrected |

# Honesty ERP UI — Component Usage Guide V2

> Canonical package: `honesty-erp-ui`  
> Rule: choose semantic behavior and compose patterns; do not reproduce their UX in feature markup.

## 1. Import map

```ts
import { ErpButton, type ErpActionPolicy } from 'honesty-erp-ui/essentials';
import { ErpIcon, type ErpIconSource } from 'honesty-erp-ui/icons';
import { ErpSelect, ErpRemoteSelect } from 'honesty-erp-ui/forms';
import { ErpSmartTable, type ErpColumnDef } from 'honesty-erp-ui/data-display';
import { ErpEntityDirectory, ErpEntityDetail } from 'honesty-erp-ui/business';
import { ErpPageShell, ErpPageHeader, ErpIconButton } from 'honesty-erp-ui';
```

Do not import the same symbol from a deprecated root facade when a canonical secondary entry point exists. Do not import internal `src/lib` files. Feature code never imports `ng-icons` directly.

## 2. Shared action model

Create an `ErpActionPolicy` for a supported action and resolve its availability in Web:

```ts
readonly saveAction: ErpActionPolicy = {
  id: 'save',
  label: 'حفظ',
  icon: 'save',
  tone: 'primary',
  variant: 'solid',
  onlineRequirement: 'online',
  busyKey: 'customer-save',
};

readonly saveAvailability = computed(() => ({
  visible: this.policy.canSave(),
  disabled: this.form.invalid || !this.policy.canSave(),
  busy: this.workflow.saving(),
  reason: this.form.invalid ? 'أكمل الحقول المطلوبة أولاً' : undefined,
}));
```

UI visibility is presentation, not security. Recheck context, branch and permission in the invocation handler before executing.

## 3. `ErpButton`

Purpose: labeled action with consistent policy, state, icon, focus and density.

Use when:

- the action needs a visible label;
- it is primary/secondary/destructive or form submit/cancel;
- busy, disabled reason or policy visibility must be represented.

Do not use when:

- the interaction is navigation text only;
- a compact, universally understood icon action is required (`ErpIconButton`);
- several low-frequency actions belong in an action menu.

Supported semantics:

- tones: primary, secondary, success, warning, danger, neutral;
- variants: solid, outline, ghost;
- sizes: sm, md, lg;
- states: hidden, disabled, busy, reason, full width.

```html
<erp-button
  [action]="saveAction"
  [availability]="saveAvailability()"
  type="submit"
  (activated)="save($event)"
/>
```

Extension point: action policy and availability only. Prohibited: feature-local `<button class="primary">` or arbitrary color/radius inputs.

## 4. `ErpIconButton`

Purpose: compact action whose semantic icon is sufficient in context.

Use for close, reveal, refresh, row overflow and compact toolbar controls. Always supply an action label; it becomes the accessible name and title. Use disclosure inputs for menu/dialog/listbox triggers.

Do not use for ambiguous business operations or a page’s primary action. Do not place raw SVG/vendor icon components in feature code.

## 5. `ErpIcon`

Purpose: render a semantic icon through the internal `ng-icons` adapter.

Use semantic names from `ErpIconSource`. The registry may map them to Fluent or another supported pack without changing feature templates. Do not use `<ng-icon>` outside the icon implementation, and do not recreate an icon database in feature code.

## 6. Text, number, password and textarea controls

Use the corresponding Forms control whenever a user edits a value. They provide CVA behavior, consistent labels, described-by/error state, disabled/readonly rendering, focus and theme behavior.

Use number controls for numeric values only; money formatting in display mode belongs to `ErpMoney`, while currency/business validation belongs to the feature form. Do not use text inputs to hide numeric semantics.

Custom extension: compose inside `ErpFormField` or register a genuine custom field renderer. Do not copy the control SCSS.

## 7. Date, time and date-time controls

Purpose: controlled Arabic-facing temporal input with stable form values.

Use the correct primitive and keep API mapping in the feature adapter. Set min/max/validation through the supported inputs. Do not rely on browser `mm/dd/yyyy` presentation and do not silently alter server timezone/date contracts.

## 8. `ErpCheckbox`, `ErpRadioGroup`, `ErpSwitch`

- Checkbox: independent boolean/multiple selection, including indeterminate selection.
- Radio Group: one value from a small, visible, mutually exclusive set.
- Switch: immediate on/off setting, not a confirmation-dependent command.

Use title/description variants for meaningful choices. Do not substitute a Select for two to four important visible choices solely to save space. Do not create custom pseudo-checkboxes.

## 9. `ErpSelect`

Purpose: local single selection with controlled panel, search, groups, icons/avatars, disabled options and no-result states.

Use when the option set is already local and bounded. Provide an operational/accessibility label even when a visible field label exists. Use semantic option metadata, not projected custom HTML for cosmetic freedom.

Do not use for server-backed unbounded search (`ErpRemoteSelect`) or multiple selection (`ErpMultiSelect`). Do not use a native feature `<select>`.

## 10. `ErpMultiSelect`

Purpose: local multiple selection with chips and clear/remove behavior.

Use for bounded option sets. Preserve a stable array value contract and provide accessible names for clear/remove actions. Avoid it for very large server sets; use a supported remote selection pattern rather than loading everything.

## 11. `ErpRemoteSelect`

Purpose: server-backed selection with typed query/load/hydration behavior, cancellation and stale-response protection.

Web owns the loader/adapter. UI receives results and emits selection/search intent. Do not inject `HttpClient` or API services into the control. Preserve identifiers separately from display labels.

## 12. `ErpDrawer`

Purpose: transient side workspace for filters, supporting edits or contextual detail.

Use logical start/end side, a concise heading, explicit close, body and footer actions. Use it for Filter Drawer and compact edit flows that do not require a route. Keep business state in the caller.

Do not use as a substitute for every page, or nest drawers without a proven workflow. Do not implement another backdrop/focus system.

## 13. `ErpModal`

Purpose: blocking decision or focused short task.

Use for confirmation, concurrency resolution and a decision that must complete before returning. Preserve Escape/outside-click policy and action hierarchy.

Do not use for long entity forms or read-only details better represented by a route/drawer. Do not create native dialogs.

## 14. `ErpTooltip`

Purpose: short supplementary label/help on hover and keyboard focus.

Use for collapsed navigation and icon actions. Tooltip content must not be the only source of required instructions or validation. Do not create title-only ad-hoc tooltips where the directive/component can be used.

## 15. Empty, Error and Loading states

Use canonical feedback surfaces:

- Empty: no-data, no-results or contextual empty condition;
- Error: failed load with retry only when a functioning retry exists;
- Loading: indeterminate/progress state with meaningful status text;
- Async Content: state orchestration around content.

An Entity Directory or Smart Table may choose when to show the state, but must not redraw it. Hide row-dependent toolbars, view switching, columns, selection and output controls when no data is displayed.

## 16. `ErpPageShell` and `ErpPageHeader`

Page Shell provides stable content/frame geometry. Page Header owns breadcrumbs, identity, subtitle/context and page actions.

Use one primary action, ordered secondary actions, then output/overflow. Put list refresh in the data toolbar, not the header. Use projected extension slots only for supported content; do not recreate page-title grids per feature.

## 17. `ErpSmartTable`

Purpose: typed table rendering, sorting intent, row selection, responsive containment and state integration.

Supply:

- column contracts;
- row identity;
- a page result and load state;
- server request/sort state;
- explicit selection capability;
- templates only for genuine cell differences.

The caller fetches data and owns query state. Smart Table must not receive URLs/services or a Customer-specific model. Do not implement pagination or total-count guesses inside a feature table.

At 1024, preserve contained horizontal scrolling. Do not force the entire page wider.

## 18. Filter Drawer

Use `ErpFilterDrawer` for committed/draft filter workflows. The feature owns the typed filter object, mapping to API query and reset defaults. The drawer owns overlay interaction and consistent apply/reset presentation.

Do not mutate live server query for every draft field unless the screen explicitly defines instant filtering. Do not place unauthorized fields in the UI and merely hide results later.

## 19. `ErpEntityDirectory`

Purpose: compose recurring ERP list UX without backend coupling.

It composes summary KPIs, filters, Smart Table/Card List, data toolbar, selection/bulk actions, output scope, pagination and canonical states. Supply `ErpEntityDirectoryConfig` and handle its discriminated `changed` intent events.

Use when a server-backed entity collection has the standard directory lifecycle. Keep DTO mapping, API calls, permission resolution and branch scope in Page/State/Adapter/Policy collaborators.

Do not use for dashboards or transactional line editors. Do not pass a service or endpoint into the config. Optional parts are opt-in and never grant authority.

## 20. `ErpStandardEntityForm`

Purpose: conventional create/edit entity workflow using schema, field registry, steps, validation, review and actions.

Use when fields and sections are predominantly conventional CRUD. Project/register custom fields and sections for real domain requirements. Keep server mapping, save workflow, concurrency and authorization in Web.

Do not force journal, payment allocation, stock movement or other complex transaction logic into an ever-growing schema. Such screens may compose primitives and domain editors directly.

## 21. `ErpEntityDetail`

Purpose: schema-guided entity hero, facts, KPIs, tabs, table/timeline/custom sections and optional information rails.

Use resolvers to derive presentation from a readonly value/context. Keep navigation/execution in the feature. Use rails only for meaningful secondary facts. Mark direction-sensitive values and allow long Arabic/identifier wrapping.

Do not put API requests into section resolvers. Do not create a rail merely to imitate a visual mockup.

## 22. KPI Card and Status Badge

KPI Card is for a measurable summary, not arbitrary content. Choose semantic tone, state, trend, progress, chips or substats; avoid consumer-provided visual values. Status Badge represents a concise state and must use the same semantic meaning consistently across features.

## 23. Action Menu, Entity/Lifecycle/Bulk/Output actions

These are placement/orchestration components over the shared action vocabulary. Use each for its semantic placement. The feature resolves availability and executes. Avoid duplicating separate permission/disabled/loading rules in each renderer.

## 24. ERP business editors

Commercial, journal, payment-allocation, stock-adjustment, report-filter, workflow and permission-tree components are domain ERP presentation. They may compose Forms/Data primitives but do not call APIs. Use them only where their business contract matches; do not treat them as generic primitives.

## 25. Prohibited feature-level bypasses

Unless implementing a UI primitive internally, feature code must not introduce:

- manually styled `<button>`, `<select>`, checkbox/radio, input or textarea when a V2 primitive matches;
- ad-hoc dropdown, modal, drawer, tooltip or empty/error/loading visual;
- direct vendor icon use;
- local copies of Smart Table, filter, pagination or action-resolution logic;
- arbitrary CSS inputs to shared components;
- API Client or `HttpClient` dependencies inside UI.

## 26. Review checklist

- Canonical entry point used.
- Accessible name and keyboard behavior verified.
- Light/Dark and RTL verified.
- 1024 width verified for page/pattern changes.
- Permission is resolved and rechecked in Web.
- Server pagination/filter/sort ownership is clear.
- Empty/loading/error states use canonical feedback.
- No feature-level native-control or icon-vendor bypass.
- Showcase is updated for a changed public contract.
- Customer Golden Reference remains green when a shared pattern changes.

- V2 Page Header
- `ErpEntityDirectory`

Use the canonical data stack.

The list must include existing Supplier functionality where currently supported:

- server paging;
- server sorting;
- server filters;
- search;
- KPI/summary if Suppliers currently requires it;
- table view;
- card view only if meaningful;
- column chooser;
- row selection;
- bulk actions;
- output/export/print;
- refresh;
- loading;
- no-data;
- no-results;
- error;
- retry.

Do not recreate toolbar/filter/pagination UX locally.

---

# 10. SUPPLIER LIST QUERY STATE

Create a typed Supplier query model.

It must explicitly model:

- page;
- page size;
- search;
- sort;
- filters;
- branch context if relevant;
- any Supplier-specific query criteria.

Rules:

- true server total count only;
- changing filter/search resets page appropriately;
- refresh preserves committed filters;
- stale requests cannot overwrite newer query state;
- branch/context change invalidates stale state;
- retry reuses the intended query;
- URL/query synchronization must remain correct if currently supported.

---

# 11. SUPPLIER ROW VIEW MODEL

Do not feed generated DTOs directly to the directory where mapping is useful.

Create a stable row view model appropriate to Supplier display.

Resolve:

- IDs;
- supplier name;
- supplier code;
- status;
- contact information;
- commercial/tax identifiers;
- branch-related presentation;
- dates;
- financial visibility if applicable.

Sensitive or unauthorized values must already be redacted/omitted before entering generic UI.

---

# 12. TABLE COLUMNS

Define Supplier columns through canonical `ErpColumnDef` contracts.

Do not write custom table markup.

Columns must:

- have stable keys;
- define sort semantics explicitly;
- define alignment appropriately;
- handle long Arabic text;
- handle LTR identifiers where necessary;
- handle phone/email direction;
- use `ErpStatusBadge`, `ErpMoney`, `ErpDateTime`, `ErpContactField`, etc. where appropriate.

Verify at:

- 1920;
- 1440;
- 1366;
- 1024.

No page-level horizontal clipping is allowed.

---

# 13. CARD VIEW

If Suppliers currently has a useful card presentation, migrate it through Directory/Card List.

Do not create a parallel feature-local card grid system.

Use a custom card template only for Supplier-specific content.

If card view provides no business value, do not add it merely because Customers has it.

---

# 14. FILTERS

Use `ErpFilterDrawer`.

Feature owns:

- draft filter model;
- committed filter model;
- defaults;
- API mapping.

Drawer owns:

- open/close;
- consistent layout;
- Apply;
- Reset;
- overlay behavior.

Do not send a server request on every draft edit unless Supplier UX explicitly requires instant filtering.

Use canonical V2 controls.

No native:

- `<select>`
- text input
- date input
- checkbox

in Supplier feature templates when an ERP control matches.

---

# 15. SUPPLIER ACTION POLICY

Create/normalize Supplier actions using the shared action vocabulary.

Potential actions must reflect actual existing Supplier behavior only.

Examples may include:

- create;
- edit;
- activate;
- deactivate;
- delete;
- print;
- export;
- refresh;
- contact-related actions;
- lifecycle actions.

For every action separate:

```text
definition
→ resolved availability
→ placement
→ invocation
→ confirmation if needed
→ execution
→ explicit result
```

Do not duplicate permission conditions in templates.

---

# 16. PERMISSIONS

Supplier UI visibility is not security.

Use the existing Web permission infrastructure.

Policy must resolve:

- action visibility;
- disabled state;
- reason;
- field visibility;
- field editability;
- sensitive financial visibility;
- branch limitations;
- lifecycle limitations.

Before executing a Supplier action:

- recheck current context;
- recheck branch;
- recheck authority as supported by existing architecture.

Do not move permission resolution into UI components.

---

# 17. BULK ACTIONS

If Suppliers supports row selection/bulk behavior:

- use Entity Directory selection;
- use Bulk Action Bar;
- show selected count;
- resolve bulk action availability explicitly;
- execute through Supplier workflow/state;
- provide partial/failure results correctly.

Do not assume every selected record can receive every action.

If the existing feature has no valid bulk workflow, do not invent one.

---

# 18. OUTPUT / PRINT / EXPORT

Migrate existing Supplier output behavior to the canonical Output surface.

Explicitly distinguish scopes where supported:

- selected;
- current page;
- all matching results.

Never treat current page as “all”.

Feature owns:

- server request;
- output query;
- filename/domain rules;
- generated file execution.

UI owns:

- format/scope selection;
- action presentation;
- intent.

Preserve permissions.

---

# 19. SUPPLIER DETAIL — ENTITY DETAIL V2

Migrate Supplier Detail to `ErpEntityDetail`.

Create a readonly Supplier detail view model/schema.

Use only actual Supplier concepts.

Possible sections, if supported by current behavior, may include:

- identity;
- commercial information;
- contact information;
- addresses;
- financial information;
- status;
- attachments;
- activity/history;
- audit;
- related entities;
- custom Supplier business sections.

Do not clone Customer sections blindly.

# 20. DETAIL LAYOUT

Use Entity Detail’s adaptive layout.

Requirements:

- no permanently empty rails;
- no wasted secondary column;
- long names/IDs/emails wrap correctly;
- phone and identifiers keep appropriate direction;
- sensitive financial information is already permission-resolved;
- 1440 and 1024 are verified.

Use custom section renderers only for real Supplier-specific sections.

---

# 21. DETAIL ACTIONS

Detail header/actions must use the same Supplier policy vocabulary as list actions.

Do not define “edit allowed” separately in List and Detail.

Create shared Supplier policy logic where domain-consistent.

Placement may differ.

Authority must not.

# 22. CREATE / EDIT — STANDARD ENTITY FORM

If Supplier Create/Edit is predominantly conventional CRUD, migrate it to:

- `ErpStandardEntityForm`

- Supplier workflow
- Supplier state
- Supplier adapter.

Do not force unusual Supplier business behavior into schema if a custom renderer is clearer.

# 23. SUPPLIER FORM MODEL

Create a feature-owned form model.

Do not directly use generated request DTO as Angular form state unless they are genuinely equivalent and the code clearly documents why.

Explicitly map:

```text
Supplier DTO
→ Supplier Form Model
→ FormGroup
→ Save Request
```

Preserve:

- IDs;

- enums/statuses;
- address/contact collections;
- upload references;
- any tax/commercial data.

# 24. FORM SCHEMA

Use schema for conventional fields.

Use the existing supported field types and custom renderer escape hatches.

Do not expand shared Form Engine with Supplier-only field types.

If Suppliers requires a complex reusable party/address/contact behavior already available in UI Business, compose that supported component.

Do not duplicate it.

---

# 25. VALIDATION

Preserve all existing Supplier business validation.

Separate:

- primitive validation;
- cross-field validation;
- business validation;
- server validation;
- transport failure.

Server validation must map into:

- matching field errors when reliable;
- validation summary otherwise.

Do not erase user-entered values on failure.

Do not maintain an unrelated duplicate error model in the template.

---

# 26. UNSAVED CHANGES

Integrate with the existing Web unsaved-change orchestration.

Rules:

- pristine navigation/cancel exits normally;
- dirty navigation/cancel requests canonical confirmation;
- choosing Stay preserves the form;
- successful save unregisters dirty state.

Header and in-form Save/Cancel must use the SAME workflow.

No alternate save path.

---

# 27. CONCURRENCY

Inspect actual Supplier API/write behavior.

If Supplier editing uses concurrency/row version:

- carry the expected token;
- detect conflict;
- use canonical Concurrency Conflict surface;
- preserve user input;
- support only actions allowed by real backend/business behavior;
- revalidate authority/token before retry.

If Suppliers genuinely has no concurrency contract, document that fact.

Do not invent one.

---
